title.zh: 卷一 本紀第一: 世紀
title.raw: 卷一 本紀第一: 世紀 Volume 1 Annals 1: Ancenstral Records

sentences.zh: 金之先，出靺鞨氏。

translations.literal: The ancestors of the Jin came forth from the Mohe clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin dynasty traced its origins to the Mohe people.

sentences.zh: 靺鞨本號勿吉。

translations.literal: Mohe was originally called Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: The Mohe had formerly been known as the Wuji.

sentences.zh: 勿吉，古肅慎地也。

translations.literal: Wuji was the territory of ancient Sushen.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuji inhabited the lands of ancient Sushen.

sentences.zh: 元魏時，勿吉有七部：曰粟末部、曰伯咄部、曰安車骨部、曰拂涅部、曰號室部、曰黑水部、曰白山部。

translations.literal: In the time of the Northern Wei, Wuji had seven divisions: the Sumo division, the Boduo division, the Anchegu division, the Funie division, the Haoshi division, the Heishui division, and the Baishan division.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Wei, the Wuji were divided into seven branches: Sumo, Boduo, Anchegu, Funie, Haoshi, Heishui, and Baishan.

sentences.zh: 隋稱靺鞨，而七部並同。

translations.literal: The Sui called them Mohe, and the seven divisions remained the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui dynasty knew them as the Mohe, and these seven divisions endured unchanged.

sentences.zh: 唐初，有黑水靺鞨、粟末靺鞨，其五部無聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tang, there were the Heishui Mohe and the Sumo Mohe; the other five divisions are not heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tang period only the Heishui Mohe and the Sumo Mohe are recorded; the fate of the other five divisions is unknown.

sentences.zh: 粟末靺鞨始附高麗，姓大氏。

translations.literal: The Sumo Mohe at first submitted to Goryeo and bore the surname Da.
translations.idiomatic: The Sumo Mohe initially allied with Goryeo and took the clan name Da.

sentences.zh: 李績破高麗，粟末靺鞨保東牟山。

translations.literal: When Li Ji defeated Goryeo, the Sumo Mohe held Dongmou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Ji’s conquest of Goryeo, the Sumo Mohe withdrew to hold Dongmou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 後爲渤海，稱王，傳十餘世。

translations.literal: Later they became Bohai, assumed kingship, and passed it down for more than ten generations.
translations.idiomatic: They later founded Bohai as a kingdom, which endured for more than ten generations.

sentences.zh: 有文字、禮樂、官府、制度。

translations.literal: They had writing, ritual and music, government offices, and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Their state possessed a written script, rites and music, an administrative apparatus, and formal institutions.

sentences.zh: 有五京、十五府、六十二州。

translations.literal: There were five capitals, fifteen prefectures, and sixty-two districts.
translations.idiomatic: Its realm comprised five capitals, fifteen prefectures, and sixty-two districts.

sentences.zh: 黑水靺鞨居肅慎地，東瀕海，南接高麗，亦附於高麗。

translations.literal: The Heishui Mohe dwelt in Sushen territory, bordered the sea on the east, adjoined Goryeo on the south, and likewise submitted to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: The Heishui Mohe lived in the old Sushen lands, with the sea to their east and Goryeo to their south, and they too were subject to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 嘗以兵十五萬衆助高麗拒唐太宗，敗于安市。

translations.literal: They once sent an army of one hundred fifty thousand men to aid Goryeo against Emperor Taizong of the Tang and were defeated at Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: They once fielded one hundred fifty thousand warriors to help Goryeo resist Tang Taizong, only to be crushed at Anshi.

sentences.zh: 開元中，來朝，置黑水府，以部長爲都督、刺史，置長史監之。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era they came to court; the Heishui Prefecture was established, tribal chiefs were made governors and prefects, and chief secretaries were appointed to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign they sent tribute to the Tang court, which created the Heishui Prefecture, appointed tribal leaders as governors and prefects, and posted chief secretaries to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 賜都督姓李氏，名獻誠，領黑水經略使。

translations.literal: The governor was granted the surname Li and the name Xian-cheng, and was made commissioner of the Heishui frontier circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ennobled the governor with the surname Li and the personal name Xian-cheng, appointing him commissioner of the Heishui frontier circuit.

sentences.zh: 其後渤海盛強，黑水役屬之，朝貢遂絕。

translations.literal: Afterward Bohai grew powerful, and Heishui became its subject; tribute to the Tang ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Bohai later rose to dominance, Heishui fell under its sway and tribute to the Tang came to an end.

sentences.zh: 五代時，契丹盡取渤海地，而黑水靺鞨附屬於契丹。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties period the Khitan seized all Bohai territory, and the Heishui Mohe submitted to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Five Dynasties the Khitan annexed the whole of Bohai, and the Heishui Mohe became subjects of the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 其在南者籍契丹，號熟女直；

translations.literal: Those in the south were registered with the Khitan and were called the “cooked” Jurchen;
translations.idiomatic: Those in the south were entered on Khitan registers and were known as the “cooked” Jurchen;

sentences.zh: 其在北者不在契丹籍，號生女直。

translations.literal: those in the north were not on Khitan registers and were called the “raw” Jurchen.
translations.idiomatic: those in the north, not entered on Khitan registers, were called the “raw” Jurchen.

sentences.zh: 生女直地有混同江、長白山，混同江亦號黑龍江，所謂「白山黑水」是也。

translations.literal: The land of the raw Jurchen had the Huntong River and Changbai Mountain; the Huntong River was also called the Black Dragon River—the so-called “White Mountain and Black Water.”
translations.idiomatic: The raw Jurchen homeland lay between the Huntong River and Changbai Mountain; the Huntong was also known as the Black Dragon River—the famed “White Mountain and Black Water.”

sentences.zh: 金之始祖諱函普，初從高麗來，年已六十餘矣。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor of the Jin, taboo name Hanpu, had first come from Goryeo when he was already more than sixty years old.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founding ancestor, whose name was Hanpu, had first arrived from Goryeo when he was already past sixty.

sentences.zh: 兄阿古乃好佛，留高麗不肯從，曰：「後世子孫必有能相聚者，吾不能去也。

translations.literal: His elder brother Agu’nai was devoted to Buddhism and remained in Goryeo, refusing to follow him, saying: “In later generations our descendants will surely be able to gather together again; I cannot leave.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Agu’nai was a devout Buddhist and stayed behind in Goryeo, refusing to accompany him. “Our descendants in ages to come will surely gather together again,” he said; “I cannot go with you.

sentences.zh: 」獨與弟保活里俱。

translations.literal: ” He alone went forth together with his younger brother Baohuoli.
translations.idiomatic: ” Only he set out together with his younger brother Baohuoli.

sentences.zh: 始祖居完顏部僕幹水之涯，保活里居耶懶。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor dwelt on the banks of the Pugan River in the Wanyan tribe; Baohuoli dwelt at Yelang.
translations.idiomatic: The founding ancestor settled on the banks of the Pugan River among the Wanyan tribe, while Baohuoli made his home at Yelang.

sentences.zh: 其後胡十門以曷蘇館歸太祖，自言其祖兄弟三人相別而去，蓋自謂阿古乃之後。

translations.literal: Later, when Hu Shimen submitted the Yisu Hall to Taizu, he declared that his forefathers were three brothers who had parted and gone their separate ways—claiming descent from Agu’nai.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Hu Shimen surrendered the Yisu Hall to Taizu, he said that his ancestors were three brothers who had separated and gone their own ways—thus claiming descent from Agu’nai.

sentences.zh: 石土門、迪古乃，保活里之裔也。

translations.literal: Shitumen and Digunai were descendants of Baohuoli.
translations.idiomatic: Shitumen and Digunai were of Baohuoli’s line.

sentences.zh: 及太祖敗遼兵於境上，獲耶律謝十，乃使梁福、斡荅刺招諭渤海人曰：「女直、渤海本同一家。

translations.literal: When Taizu defeated Liao forces on the border and captured Yelü Xie-shi, he sent Liang Fu and Wodaci to summon the Bohai people, saying: “Jurchen and Bohai are originally one family.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu routed the Liao army on the frontier and captured Yelü Xie-shi, he dispatched Liang Fu and Wodaci to proclaim to the Bohai people: “The Jurchen and the Bohai were originally one people.

sentences.zh: 」蓋其初皆勿吉之七部也。

translations.literal: ” For in the beginning they had all been among the seven divisions of Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: ” In origin they had all belonged to the seven Wuji divisions.

sentences.zh: 始祖至完顏部，居久之，其部人嘗殺它族之人，由是兩族交惡，哄鬥不能解。

translations.literal: When the founding ancestor came to the Wanyan tribe and dwelt there for a long time, men of the tribe once killed a man of another clan; the two clans became hostile and brawled without end.
translations.idiomatic: After the founding ancestor settled among the Wanyan tribe, some of its men killed a man from another clan; the two groups turned hostile and fought incessantly without resolution.

sentences.zh: 完顏部人謂始祖曰：「若能爲部人解此怨，使兩族不相殺，部有賢女，年六十而未嫁，當以相配，仍爲同部。

translations.literal: The Wanyan tribesmen said to the founding ancestor: “If you can settle this feud for the tribe so that the two clans no longer kill one another, there is a worthy woman in the tribe, sixty years old and still unmarried—we will give her to you in marriage and make you of the same tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Wanyan people said to the founding ancestor: “If you can end this feud so our clans cease killing one another, there is an esteemed woman in our tribe, sixty years old and still unwed—we will give her to you in marriage and reckon you as one of us.

sentences.zh: 」始祖曰：「諾。

translations.literal: ” The founding ancestor said: “Agreed.
translations.idiomatic: ” The founding ancestor replied: “Very well.

sentences.zh: 」乃自往諭之曰：「殺一人而鬥不解，損傷益多。

translations.literal: ” He then went in person to admonish them, saying: “If you kill one man and the fighting does not cease, the wounded and dead will only increase.
translations.idiomatic: ” He went himself to counsel both sides: “Slay one man and the feud still will not end; the dead and wounded will only multiply.

sentences.zh: 曷若止誅首亂者一人，部內以物納償汝，可以無鬥，而且獲利焉。

translations.literal: Why not execute only the chief troublemaker, and let the tribe pay compensation in goods to you? Then there need be no fighting, and you will profit besides.
translations.idiomatic: Why not put to death only the ringleader, and let the tribe pay the aggrieved party in goods? Fighting would cease, and you would gain besides.

sentences.zh: 」怨家從之。

translations.literal: ” The aggrieved clan assented.
translations.idiomatic: ” The injured party agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃爲約曰：「凡有殺傷人者，征其家人口一、馬十偶、牸牛十、黃金六兩，與所殺傷之家，即兩解，不得私鬥。

translations.literal: He then made a covenant, saying: “Whoever kills or wounds another shall pay one member of his household, ten teams of horses, ten cows, and six taels of gold to the injured household; then both sides shall be reconciled and may not fight privately.
translations.idiomatic: He established a pact: “Whoever kills or injures another must pay the victim’s family one household member, ten teams of horses, ten cows, and six taels of gold; the matter is then settled and private vengeance is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「謹如約。

translations.literal: ” They said: “We shall strictly observe the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: ” They answered: “We shall abide strictly by the pact.

sentences.zh: 」女直之俗，殺人償馬牛三十，自此始。

translations.literal: ” Among Jurchen custom, thirty horses and cattle were paid for a killing—from this it began.
translations.idiomatic: ” Thus began the Jurchen custom of paying thirty horses and cattle as blood-price for a killing.

sentences.zh: 既備償如約，部衆信服之，謝以青牛一，並許歸六十之婦。

translations.literal: When compensation had been paid according to the covenant, the tribesmen trusted him; they thanked him with one black ox and also granted him the woman of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Once the compensation was paid as agreed, the tribe trusted him; they presented a black ox in gratitude and also gave him the sixty-year-old woman in marriage.

sentences.zh: 始祖乃以青牛爲聘禮而納之，並得其貲產。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor then took the black ox as betrothal gift and married her, and thereby obtained her property as well.
translations.idiomatic: The founding ancestor accepted the black ox as betrothal gift and wed her, gaining her possessions along with her.

sentences.zh: 後生二男，長曰烏魯，次曰斡魯，一女曰注思板，遂爲完顏部人。

translations.literal: Later she bore two sons—the elder named Wulu, the younger named Walu—and one daughter named Zhusi-ban; thus he became a man of the Wanyan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: She later bore two sons, Wulu and Walu, and a daughter named Zhusi-ban, and he was thereby enrolled among the Wanyan people.

sentences.zh: 天會十四年，追諡景元皇帝，廟號始祖。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously titled Emperor Jingyuan, with the temple name Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he received the posthumous title Emperor Jingyuan, with the temple name Shizu (Founding Ancestor).

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏曰光陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named Guang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong his tomb was designated Guang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡始祖懿憲景元皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his posthumous title was augmented to Emperor Yixian Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was expanded to Emperor Yixian Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 子德帝，諱烏魯。

translations.literal: His son, the Virtuous Emperor, taboo name Wulu.
translations.idiomatic: His son, the Virtuous Emperor, whose name was Wulu.

sentences.zh: 天會十四年，追諡德皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously titled the Virtuous Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously titled the Virtuous Emperor.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏曰熙陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named Xi Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong his tomb was named Xi Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡淵穆玄德皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his posthumous title was augmented to Emperor Yuanmu Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was expanded to Emperor Yuanmu Xuande.

sentences.zh: 子安帝，諱跋海。

translations.literal: His son, the Peaceful Emperor, taboo name Bahai.
translations.idiomatic: His son, the Peaceful Emperor, whose name was Bahai.

sentences.zh: 天會十四年，追諡安皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously titled the Peaceful Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously titled the Peaceful Emperor.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏建陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named Jian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong his tomb was designated Jian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡和靖慶安皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his posthumous title was augmented to Emperor Hejing Qing’an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was expanded to Emperor Hejing Qing’an.

sentences.zh: 子獻祖，諱綏可。

translations.literal: His son, the Offering Ancestor, taboo name Shuike.
translations.idiomatic: His son, the Offering Ancestor, whose name was Shuike.

sentences.zh: 黑水舊俗無室廬，負山水坎地，梁木其上，覆以土，夏則出隨水草以居，冬則入處其中，遷徙不常。

translations.literal: By the old customs of Heishui there were no houses; people leaned timbers against hillsides in hollow ground, covered them with earth, went out in summer following grass and water to live, and in winter dwelt within these structures, moving constantly.
translations.idiomatic: In the old Heishui way there were no fixed dwellings: people set timbers against hillsides in hollows, roofed them with earth, ranged abroad in summer following pasture and water, and in winter lived inside these shelters, ever on the move.

sentences.zh: 獻祖乃徙居海古水，耕墾樹藝，始築室，有棟宇之制，人呼其地爲納葛里。

translations.literal: The Offering Ancestor then moved to the Haigu River, plowed fields and planted trees, and for the first time built houses with a framework of beams and rafters; people called that place Nageli.
translations.idiomatic: The Offering Ancestor relocated to the Haigu River, opened fields for cultivation, and for the first time erected framed dwellings; the place was called Nageli.

sentences.zh: 納葛里者，漢語居室也。

translations.literal: Nageli means “dwelling-place” in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Nageli means “dwelling” in Chinese—the name for a settled home.

sentences.zh: 自此遂定居于安出虎水之側矣。

translations.literal: From this they permanently settled on the banks of the Anchuhu River.
translations.idiomatic: From that time they established a permanent settlement on the banks of the Anchuhu River.

sentences.zh: 天會十四年，追諡定昭皇帝，廟號獻祖。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously titled Emperor Dingzhao, with the temple name Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he received the posthumous title Emperor Dingzhao, with the temple name Xianzu (Offering Ancestor).

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏曰輝陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named Hui Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong his tomb was named Hui Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡獻祖純烈定昭皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his posthumous title was augmented to Emperor Chunlie Dingzhao of the Offering Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was expanded to Offering Ancestor Emperor Chunlie Dingzhao.

sentences.zh: 子昭祖，諱石魯，剛毅質直。

translations.literal: His son, the Bright Ancestor, taboo name Shilu, was firm, resolute, and plain in character.
translations.idiomatic: His son, the Bright Ancestor, named Shilu, was stern, resolute, and unadorned in nature.

sentences.zh: 生女直無書契，無約束，不可檢制。

translations.literal: The raw Jurchen had no written records and no binding rules; they could not be regulated or controlled.
translations.idiomatic: The raw Jurchen kept no written records and observed no fixed laws; they could scarcely be governed at all.

sentences.zh: 昭祖欲稍立條教，諸父、部人皆不悅，欲坑殺之。

translations.literal: The Bright Ancestor wished to establish regulations little by little; the elders and tribesmen were all displeased and wanted to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Ancestor sought gradually to impose basic regulations; the tribal elders were displeased and plotted to kill him.

sentences.zh: 已被執，叔父謝里忽知部衆將殺昭祖，曰：「吾兄子，賢人也，必能承家，安輯部衆，此輩奈何輒欲坑殺之！

translations.literal: After he had been seized, his uncle Shelihu, learning that the tribesmen intended to kill the Bright Ancestor, said: “He is my brother’s son, a worthy man who can surely uphold our house and bring peace to the tribe—how can you casually wish to kill him!
translations.idiomatic: Once he was seized, his uncle Shelihu, hearing that the tribe meant to execute the Bright Ancestor, cried out: “He is my brother’s son—a man of talent who can sustain our line and settle the tribe. How dare you think to murder him!

sentences.zh: 」亟往，彎弓注矢射於衆中，劫執者皆散走，昭祖乃得免。

translations.literal: ” He hurried thither, bent his bow, and shot arrows into the crowd; those who held him captive all scattered, and the Bright Ancestor was spared.
translations.idiomatic: ” He rushed forward, strung his bow, and loosed arrows into the throng; his captors fled in all directions, and the Bright Ancestor escaped death.

sentences.zh: 昭祖稍以條教爲治，部落浸強。

translations.literal: The Bright Ancestor gradually governed by regulations, and the tribe grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: As the Bright Ancestor slowly imposed order through regulations, the tribe steadily grew in strength.

sentences.zh: 遼以惕隱官之。

translations.literal: The Liao appointed him a tiyin official.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao court invested him with the office of tiyin.

sentences.zh: 諸部猶以舊俗，不肯用條教。

translations.literal: The various tribes still clung to old customs and would not accept regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Other tribes still clung to their old ways and refused to submit to his regulations.

sentences.zh: 昭祖耀武至於青嶺、白山，順者撫之，不從者討伐之，入于蘇濱、耶懶之地，所至克捷，還經僕燕水。

translations.literal: The Bright Ancestor displayed martial prowess as far as Qing Ridge and White Mountain; those who submitted he comforted, those who did not he attacked and punished, penetrating the lands of Subin and Yelang, victorious wherever he went; on his return he passed the Puyan River.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Ancestor campaigned as far as Qing Ridge and White Mountain: he won over the compliant and chastised the defiant, advancing into Subin and Yelang and prevailing wherever he struck; on the homeward march he crossed the Puyan River.

sentences.zh: 僕燕，漢語惡瘡也。

translations.literal: Puyan means “festering sores” in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Puyan means “festering sores” in Chinese—a name he found ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 昭祖惡其地名，雖已困憊，不肯止。

translations.literal: The Bright Ancestor detested the place-name; though already exhausted, he would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Though his men were spent, he would not halt in that inauspiciously named place.

sentences.zh: 行至姑里甸，得疾。

translations.literal: When he reached Guli Ford he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Guli Ford, he fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 迨夜，寢於村舍。

translations.literal: By nightfall he lodged in a village house.
translations.idiomatic: As night fell he took shelter in a village dwelling.

sentences.zh: 有盜至，遂中夜啟行，至逼剌紀村止焉。

translations.literal: Thieves came, and at midnight he set out again, halting at Bila Village.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves appeared, and at midnight he broke camp again, stopping at Bila Village.

sentences.zh: 是夕，卒。

translations.literal: That night he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same night.

sentences.zh: 載柩而行，遇賊于路，奪柩去。

translations.literal: They bore the coffin onward, but on the road met bandits who seized the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: As the coffin was borne homeward, bandits waylaid the procession and carried it off.

sentences.zh: 部衆追賊與戰，復得柩。

translations.literal: The tribesmen pursued the bandits and fought; they recovered the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: The tribe pursued, fought the robbers, and won the coffin back.

sentences.zh: 加古部人蒲虎復來襲之，垂及，蒲虎問諸路人曰：「石魯柩去此幾何？

translations.literal: Puhu of the Jagü tribe came to attack again; when he was almost upon them, Puhu asked passersby: “How far has Shilu’s coffin gone from here?
translations.idiomatic: Puhu of the Jagü tribe attacked once more; as he drew near, he asked travelers on the road: “How far ahead is Shilu’s coffin?

sentences.zh: 」其人曰：「遠矣，追之不及也。

translations.literal: ” The man said: “It is far off; you cannot overtake it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Someone answered: “It is far ahead; you cannot catch up.

sentences.zh: 」蒲虎遂止。

translations.literal: ” Puhu then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ” Puhu thereupon gave up the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 於是乃得歸葬焉。

translations.literal: Only then were they able to return and bury him.
translations.idiomatic: At last they were able to bring the coffin home and bury him.

sentences.zh: 生女直之俗，至昭祖時稍用條教，民頗聽從，尚未有文字，無官府，不知歲月晦朔，是以年壽修短莫得而考焉。

translations.literal: In Jurchen custom, it was only from the time of the Bright Ancestor that regulations were somewhat followed and the people largely obeyed; there was as yet no writing, no government offices, and no knowledge of months, new moons, or intercalation—thus their ages and lifespans cannot be ascertained.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Jurchen it was only from the Bright Ancestor’s day that tribal regulations took hold and the people largely obeyed; writing, offices, and the reckoning of months and years were still unknown—so the length of their lives cannot be determined.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，追諡成襄皇帝，廟號昭祖。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously titled Emperor Chengxiang, with the temple name Zhaozu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he received the posthumous title Emperor Chengxiang, with the temple name Zhaozu (Bright Ancestor).

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，藏號安陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named An Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong his tomb was designated An Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡昭祖武惠成襄皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his posthumous title was augmented to Bright Ancestor Emperor Wuhui Chengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was expanded to Bright Ancestor Emperor Wuhui Chengxiang.

sentences.zh: 子景祖，諱烏古乃。

translations.literal: His son, the Accomplished Ancestor, taboo name Wugu.
translations.idiomatic: His son, the Accomplished Ancestor, whose name was Wugu.

sentences.zh: 遼太平元年辛酉歲生。

translations.literal: He was born in the xinyou year of the first year of Liao Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the xinyou year, the first year of Liao Taiping (1081).

sentences.zh: 自始祖至此，已六世矣。

translations.literal: From the founding ancestor to this point, six generations had passed.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding ancestor to his time, six generations had elapsed.

sentences.zh: 景祖稍役屬諸部，自白山、耶悔、統門、耶懶、土骨論之屬，以至五國之長，皆聽命。

translations.literal: The Accomplished Ancestor gradually brought the tribes under his authority—from White Mountain, Yehui, Tongmen, Yelang, Tugulun, and their kind, down to the chiefs of the Five States, all obeyed his command.
translations.idiomatic: The Accomplished Ancestor gradually subordinated the surrounding tribes: from White Mountain, Yehui, Tongmen, Yelang, and Tugulun to the chiefs of the Five States—all came under his authority.

sentences.zh: 是時，遼之邊民有逃而歸者。

translations.literal: At that time Liao frontier people who fled returned to the Jurchen.
translations.idiomatic: About this time Liao subjects on the frontier fled Liao rule and came over to the Jurchen.

sentences.zh: 及遼以兵徙鐵勒、烏惹之民，鐵勒、烏惹多不肯徙，亦逃而來歸。

translations.literal: When the Liao used troops to relocate the Tiele and Wunü peoples, many of the Tiele and Wunü refused to move and likewise fled and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao sought to relocate the Tiele and Wunü by force, many refused to move and fled to the Jurchen instead.

sentences.zh: 遼使曷魯林牙將兵來索逋逃之民。

translations.literal: The Liao sent the Yelu Helin ya to lead troops to demand the return of the fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao dispatched the Yelu Helin ya at the head of an army to reclaim the fugitives.

sentences.zh: 景祖恐遼兵深入，盡得山川道路險易，或將圖之，乃以計止之曰：「兵若深入，諸部必驚擾，變生不測，逋戶亦不可得，非計也。

translations.literal: The Accomplished Ancestor feared that if Liao troops penetrated deeply they would learn all the mountains, rivers, roads, and defiles, and might then plot against him; he therefore stopped them by stratagem, saying: “If your army advances deep into our lands, the tribes will surely be alarmed and unforeseen troubles may arise; you will not recover the fugitives either—it is no good plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Accomplished Ancestor feared that a deep Liao incursion would expose every mountain pass, river, and road to them and invite future designs against him; he therefore dissuaded them, saying: “If your army pushes deep into our country, the tribes will panic and unforeseen troubles will arise—you will recover no fugitives, and the venture is unwise.

sentences.zh: 」曷魯以爲然，遂止其軍，與曷魯自行索之。

translations.literal: ” Helin thought this reasonable and halted his army; he and Helin went in person to search for them.
translations.idiomatic: ” Helin agreed, held back his main force, and went with the Accomplished Ancestor in person to hunt down the fugitives.

sentences.zh: 是時，鄰部雖稍從，孩懶水烏林答部石顯尚拒阻不服。

translations.literal: Though neighboring tribes now submitted somewhat, Shixian of the Wulinzha tribe on the Hailan River still resisted and would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Though neighboring tribes were gradually coming under his sway, Shixian of the Hailan River Wulinzha tribe still held out in defiance.

sentences.zh: 攻之，不克。

translations.literal: They attacked him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: An attack failed to subdue him.

sentences.zh: 景祖以計告於遼主，遼主遣使責讓石顯。

translations.literal: The Accomplished Ancestor informed the Liao sovereign of his stratagem, and the Liao sovereign sent envoys to rebuke Shixian.
translations.idiomatic: The Accomplished Ancestor laid his plan before the Liao emperor, who sent envoys to reprimand Shixian.

sentences.zh: 石顯乃遣其子婆諸刊入朝，遼主厚賜遣還。

translations.literal: Shixian then sent his son Pojukan to court; the Liao sovereign richly rewarded him and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian thereupon sent his son Pojukan to the Liao court, where the emperor lavished gifts upon him and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 其後石顯與婆諸刊入見遼主於春蒐。

translations.literal: Later Shixian and Pojukan went to see the Liao sovereign at the spring hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shixian and Pojukan attended the Liao emperor at the spring hunt.

sentences.zh: 遼主乃留石顯於邊地，而遣婆諸刊還所部。

translations.literal: The Liao sovereign detained Shixian on the frontier and sent Pojukan back to his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor detained Shixian on the frontier while sending Pojukan back to his people.

sentences.zh: 景祖之謀也。

translations.literal: This was the Accomplished Ancestor’s stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: All of this was the Accomplished Ancestor’s design.

sentences.zh: 既而五國蒲聶部節度使拔乙門叛遼，鷹路不通。

translations.literal: Before long, Bayimen, military commissioner of the Punie tribe among the Five States, rebelled against the Liao, and the hawk-tribute route was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Bayimen, commissioner of the Punie tribe among the Five States, rebelled against the Liao, severing the hawk-tribute route.

sentences.zh: 遼人將討之，先遣同幹來諭旨。

translations.literal: The Liao were about to campaign against him and first sent Tonggan to announce the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: As the Liao prepared to punish him, they first dispatched Tonggan to convey the court’s orders.

sentences.zh: 景祖曰：「可以計取。

translations.literal: The Accomplished Ancestor said: “He can be taken by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The Accomplished Ancestor said: “He can be seized by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 若用兵，彼將走保險阻，非歲月可平也。

translations.literal: If you use force, he will flee to rugged strongholds, and it will not be pacified within months.
translations.idiomatic: If you march against him, he will flee into mountain fastnesses and cannot be subdued in mere months.

sentences.zh: 」遼人從之。

translations.literal: ” The Liao assented.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Liao accepted this counsel.

sentences.zh: 蓋景祖終畏遼兵之入其境也，故自以爲功。

translations.literal: For the Accomplished Ancestor always feared Liao troops entering his territory; he therefore took credit for the plan himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Accomplished Ancestor had always dreaded a Liao invasion of his lands, and so he claimed the stratagem as his own achievement.

sentences.zh: 於是景祖陽與拔乙門爲好，而以妻子爲質，襲而擒之，獻於遼主。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Accomplished Ancestor pretended friendship with Bayimen, gave his wife and children as hostages, then attacked and captured him and presented him to the Liao sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned friendship with Bayimen, left his wife and children as hostages, then struck and seized him and delivered him to the Liao emperor.

sentences.zh: 遼主召見於寢殿，燕賜加等，以爲生女直部族節度使。

translations.literal: The Liao sovereign summoned him to the sleeping hall, entertained him with a feast and extraordinary gifts, and made him military commissioner of the raw Jurchen tribal confederation.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor received him in the private hall, feasted him with exceptional honors, and appointed him military commissioner over the raw Jurchen tribes.

sentences.zh: 遼人呼節度使爲太師，金人稱都太師者自此始。

translations.literal: The Liao called a military commissioner “Grand Master”; the Jin title “Grand Master of the Capital” began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao styled a military commissioner “Grand Master”; from this time the Jin began to use the title “Grand Master of the Capital.”

sentences.zh: 遼主將刻印與之，景祖不肯系遼籍，辭曰：「請俟他日。

translations.literal: When the Liao sovereign was about to engrave a seal and grant it to him, the Accomplished Ancestor refused to be entered on Liao registers, declining: “Please wait for another day.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao emperor prepared to cast a seal and enroll him on the Liao registers, the Accomplished Ancestor refused, saying: “Let that wait for another day.

sentences.zh: 」遼主終欲與之，遣使來。

translations.literal: ” The Liao sovereign still wished to grant it and sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor still insisted on granting the seal and sent envoys again.

sentences.zh: 景祖詭使部人揚言曰：「主公若受印系籍，部人必殺之！

translations.literal: The Accomplished Ancestor secretly had tribesmen spread word, saying: “If our lord accepts the seal and enters the registers, the tribe will surely kill him!
translations.idiomatic: He secretly had his people spread the rumor: “If our lord accepts the seal and enters the Liao registers, the tribe will kill him!

sentences.zh: 」用是以拒之，遼使乃還。

translations.literal: ” By this means he refused, and the Liao envoys returned.
translations.idiomatic: ” On this pretext he declined, and the Liao envoys withdrew.

sentences.zh: 既爲節度使，有官屬，紀綱漸立矣。

translations.literal: Once he became military commissioner, he had officials, and order was gradually established.
translations.idiomatic: As military commissioner he acquired a staff, and governmental order was gradually established.

sentences.zh: 生女直舊無鐵，鄰國有以甲胄來鬻者，傾貲厚賈以與貿易，亦令昆弟族人皆售之。

translations.literal: The raw Jurchen formerly had no iron; when neighboring states offered armor for sale, he spent his wealth to buy it in trade and also had brothers and clansmen sell theirs.
translations.idiomatic: The raw Jurchen had long lacked iron; when neighbors offered armor for sale, he poured out his wealth to buy it and had kinsmen trade theirs as well.

sentences.zh: 得鐵既多，因之以修弓矢，備器械，兵勢稍振，前後願附者衆。

translations.literal: When iron grew plentiful, he thereby fashioned bows and arrows and prepared weapons; military strength gradually revived, and many came to submit before and after.
translations.idiomatic: With iron in abundance he forged bows and arrows and stocked arms; his forces grew stronger, and tribes submitted to him in growing numbers.

sentences.zh: 斡泯水蒲察部、泰神忒保水完顏部、統門水溫蒂痕部、神隱水完顏部，皆相繼來附。

translations.literal: The Pucha tribe on the Womin River, the Wanyan tribe on the Taishen-tebao River, the Wendihan tribe on the Tongmen River, and the Wanyan tribe on the Shenyin River all came to submit in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Pucha on the Womin, the Wanyan on the Taishen-tebao, the Wendihan on the Tongmen, and another Wanyan branch on the Shenyin all submitted in turn.

sentences.zh: 景祖爲人寬恕，能容物，平生不見喜慍。

translations.literal: The Accomplished Ancestor was forgiving in nature, able to bear with others, and throughout his life showed neither joy nor anger.
translations.idiomatic: The Accomplished Ancestor was magnanimous and forbearing; in all his days he was never seen to show joy or anger.

sentences.zh: 推財與人，分食解衣，無所吝惜。

translations.literal: He gave away wealth to others, shared food and stripped off his garments—nothing did he begrudge.
translations.idiomatic: He gave away his goods freely, shared his food, and even parted with his clothing without stint.

sentences.zh: 人或忤之，亦不念。

translations.literal: If anyone offended him, he did not bear it in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wronged him he did not hold to account.

sentences.zh: 先時，有叛去者，遣人諭誘之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when some had rebelled and left, he sent men to persuade and entice them back.
translations.idiomatic: When men had once rebelled and fled, he sent envoys to coax them home.

sentences.zh: 叛者曰：「汝主，活羅也。

translations.literal: The rebel said: “Your lord is a Huoluo.
translations.idiomatic: One deserter replied: “Your master is a Huoluo.

sentences.zh: 活羅，吾能獲之，吾豈能爲活羅屈哉！

translations.literal: A Huoluo—I can catch one; how could I bow to a Huoluo!
translations.idiomatic: A Huoluo—I can snare one myself. Why should I submit to a Huoluo!

sentences.zh: 」活羅，漢語慈烏也。

translations.literal: ” Huoluo means “benevolent crow” in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: ” Huoluo means “benevolent crow” in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 北方有之，狀如大雞，善啄物，見馬牛橐駝脊間有瘡，啄其脊間食之，馬牛輒死，若饑不得食，雖砂石亦食之。

translations.literal: It exists in the north, shaped like a large fowl, skilled at pecking; when it sees sores on the backs of horses, oxen, or camels it pecks the sores and eats them, and the beasts die; if hungry and unable to find food, it will even eat sand and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Found in the north, it is the size of a large fowl and a relentless scavenger: it pecks at sores on horses, cattle, and camels until the beasts die; in famine it will devour even sand and gravel.

sentences.zh: 景祖嗜酒好色，飲啖過人，時人呼曰活羅，故彼以此訕之，亦不以介意。

translations.literal: The Accomplished Ancestor was fond of wine and women and ate and drank beyond others; people of the time called him Huoluo, so they mocked him with this, yet he took no offense.
translations.idiomatic: The Accomplished Ancestor loved wine and women and out-ate and out-drank all others; contemporaries nicknamed him Huoluo, and his enemies mocked him with the name—yet he was unperturbed.

sentences.zh: 其後訕者力屈來降，厚賜遣還。

translations.literal: Later, when the mocker’s strength was spent, he came to submit and was richly rewarded and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: When the taunter’s strength was broken, he submitted and was richly rewarded and sent home.

sentences.zh: 曷懶水有率衆降者，錄其歲月姓名，即遣去，俾復其故。

translations.literal: When a leader on the Halian River came with his followers to submit, he recorded their names and the month and year, then sent them away to restore their former status.
translations.idiomatic: When a Halian River chief surrendered with his followers, he recorded names and dates, then sent them back to their former standing.

sentences.zh: 人以此益信服之。

translations.literal: People therefore trusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The people’s faith in him deepened accordingly.

sentences.zh: 遼鹹雍八年，五國沒拈部謝野勃堇叛遼，鷹路不通。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Liao Xianyong, Xieye, a chief of the Monian tribe among the Five States, rebelled against the Liao, and the hawk route was again cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Liao Xianyong, Chief Xieye of the Monian tribe among the Five States rebelled, once again blocking the hawk-tribute route.

sentences.zh: 景祖伐之，謝野來禦。

translations.literal: The Accomplished Ancestor campaigned against him; Xieye came out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The Accomplished Ancestor marched against him; Xieye met him in battle.

sentences.zh: 景祖被重鎧，率衆力戰。

translations.literal: The Accomplished Ancestor donned heavy armor and led his men in fierce fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Clad in heavy armor, the Accomplished Ancestor led his warriors in hard fighting.

sentences.zh: 謝野兵敗，走拔里邁濼。

translations.literal: Xieye’s army was defeated and fled toward the Boli Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Xieye was defeated and fled toward the Boli Marsh.

sentences.zh: 時方十月，冰忽解，謝野不能軍，衆皆潰去，乃旋師。

translations.literal: It was then the tenth month, yet the ice suddenly broke up; Xieye could not keep his army together, his men all scattered, and he turned his forces back.
translations.idiomatic: Though it was only the tenth month, the ice thawed without warning; Xieye could not hold his army together, his troops scattered, and the Jurchen withdrew.

sentences.zh: 道中遇逋亡，要遮險阻，晝夜拒戰，比至部已憊。

translations.literal: On the road they met fugitives who barred the passes and fought day and night; by the time they reached the tribe they were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: On the homeward march fugitives blocked the defiles and fought day and night; when they reached home the army was spent.

sentences.zh: 即往見遼邊將達魯骨，自陳敗謝野功。

translations.literal: He then went to see the Liao frontier general Dalugu and reported his victory over Xieye.
translations.idiomatic: He went at once to the Liao frontier commander Dalugu to report his defeat of Xieye.

sentences.zh: 行次來流水，未見達魯骨，疾作而復，卒於家，年五十四。

translations.literal: En route at the Laishui River, before he could see Dalugu, his illness relapsed and he recovered briefly, then died at home, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: On the march at Laishui River, before he could reach Dalugu, his illness returned; he died at home, aged fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 天會十四年，追諡惠桓皇帝，廟號景祖。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously titled Emperor Huihuan, with the temple name Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he received the posthumous title Emperor Huihuan, with the temple name Jingzu.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，藏號定陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named Ding Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong his tomb was designated Ding Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡景祖英烈惠桓皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his posthumous title was augmented to Accomplished Ancestor Emperor Yinglie Huihuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was expanded to Accomplished Ancestor Emperor Yinglie Huihuan.

sentences.zh: 第二子襲節度使，是爲世祖，諱劾里缽。

translations.literal: His second son succeeded to the military commissionership; this was the World Ancestor, taboo name Helibo.
translations.idiomatic: His second son inherited the commissionership—this was the World Ancestor, whose name was Helibo.

sentences.zh: 生女直之俗，生子年長即異居。

translations.literal: By Jurchen custom, when sons reached maturity they lived apart.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Jurchen, grown sons customarily established separate households.

sentences.zh: 景祖九子，元配唐括氏生劾者，次世祖，次劾孫，次肅宗，次穆宗。

translations.literal: The Accomplished Ancestor had nine sons; his primary consort of the Tangut clan bore Hezhe, next the World Ancestor, next Hesun, next the Solemn Ancestor, and next the Mournful Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The Accomplished Ancestor had nine sons. His principal wife of the Tangut clan bore Hezhe, then the World Ancestor, Hesun, the Solemn Ancestor, and the Mournful Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 及當異居，景祖曰：「劾者柔和，可治家務。

translations.literal: When the time came to live apart, the Accomplished Ancestor said: “Hezhe is gentle and can manage household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When they were to divide households, the Accomplished Ancestor said: “Hezhe is mild and fit to manage the home.

sentences.zh: 劾里缽有器量智識，何事不成。

translations.literal: Helibo has capacity and wisdom; what undertaking could he not accomplish?
translations.idiomatic: Helibo has judgment and foresight; what task could he not achieve?

sentences.zh: 劾孫亦柔善人耳。

translations.literal: Hesun too is a gentle and good man.
translations.idiomatic: Hesun is likewise a gentle and upright man.

sentences.zh: 」乃命劾者與世祖同居，劾孫與肅宗同居。

translations.literal: ” He therefore ordered Hezhe to dwell with the World Ancestor, and Hesun with the Solemn Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: ” He ordered Hezhe to remain with the World Ancestor and Hesun with the Solemn Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 景祖卒，世祖繼之。

translations.literal: When the Accomplished Ancestor died, the World Ancestor succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Accomplished Ancestor died, the World Ancestor took his place.

sentences.zh: 世祖卒，肅宗繼之。

translations.literal: When the World Ancestor died, the Solemn Ancestor succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the World Ancestor died, the Solemn Ancestor succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 肅宗卒，穆宗繼之。

translations.literal: When the Solemn Ancestor died, the Mournful Ancestor succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Solemn Ancestor died, the Mournful Ancestor succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 穆宗復傳世祖之子，至於太祖，竟登大位焉。

translations.literal: The Mournful Ancestor in turn passed the line to the World Ancestor’s son, until Taizu at last ascended the great throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Mournful Ancestor then passed leadership to the World Ancestor’s line, until Taizu finally claimed the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 世祖，遼重熙八年己卯歲生。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor was born in the jimao year, the eighth year of Liao Chongxi.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor was born in the jimao year of Liao Chongxi’s eighth year (1039).

sentences.zh: 遼鹹雍十年，襲節度使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Liao Xianyong he inherited the military commissionership.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Liao Xianyong he inherited the military commissionership.

sentences.zh: 景祖異母弟跋黑有異志，世祖慮其爲變，加意事之，不使將兵，但爲部長。

translations.literal: The Accomplished Ancestor’s younger half-brother Bahei harbored divergent ambitions; the World Ancestor, fearing he might stir trouble, treated him with special care, never letting him command troops but only making him a tribal chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Accomplished Ancestor’s half-brother Bahei nursed rebellious designs; the World Ancestor, fearing revolt, treated him with unusual deference, never entrusting him with troops but only making him a tribal chief.

sentences.zh: 跋黑遂誘桓赧、散達、烏春、窩謀罕爲亂，及間諸部使貳于世祖。

translations.literal: Bahei then incited Huanran, Sandá, Wuchun, and Womouhan to rebel, and sowed division among the tribes to make them turn against the World Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Bahei incited Huanran, Sandá, Wuchun, and Womouhan to rise in revolt and worked among the tribes to turn them against the World Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 世祖猶欲撫慰之，語在跋黑、桓赧等傳中。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor still wished to appease them; the account is in the biographies of Bahei, Huanran, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor still sought to conciliate them; the full account appears in the biographies of Bahei, Huanran, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗買加古部鍛工烏不屯被甲九十，烏春欲托此以爲兵端，世祖還其甲，語在《烏春傳》。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor once bought ninety suits of armor from Wubutun, an armorer of the Jagü tribe; Wuchun wished to use this as a pretext for war, but the World Ancestor returned the armor—the account is in the “Biography of Wuchun.”
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor once purchased ninety suits of armor from Wubutun, an armorer of the Jagü tribe; Wuchun tried to turn this into a casus belli, but the World Ancestor returned the armor—the story is told in the “Biography of Wuchun.”

sentences.zh: 部中有流言曰：「欲生則附于跋黑，欲死則附於劾里缽、頗剌淑。

translations.literal: A rumor spread in the tribe: “If you wish to live, attach yourself to Bahei; if you wish to die, attach yourself to Helibo and Pilashi.
translations.idiomatic: A saying circulated in the tribe: “Want to live—follow Bahei; want to die—follow Helibo and Pilashi.

sentences.zh: 」世祖聞之，疑焉。

translations.literal: ” When the World Ancestor heard this, he was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: ” The World Ancestor heard this and grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 無以察之，乃佯爲具裝，欲有所往者，陰遣人揚言曰：「寇至！

translations.literal: Unable to investigate directly, he pretended to arm for departure, then secretly had men spread word: “Bandits have come!
translations.idiomatic: Unable to test loyalties openly, he feigned a muster for campaign and secretly spread the alarm: “Enemies are upon us!

sentences.zh: 」部衆聞者莫知虛實，有保于跋黑之室者，有保于世祖之室者，世祖乃盡得兄弟部屬向背彼此之情矣。

translations.literal: ” Those who heard in the tribe did not know truth from falsehood; some took refuge in Bahei’s house, some in the World Ancestor’s—and thus he learned completely where brothers, tribesmen, and followers stood with one another.
translations.idiomatic: ” The tribesmen could not tell rumor from reality; some fled to Bahei’s house, others to the World Ancestor’s—and so he learned exactly who stood with whom among brothers, clans, and followers.

sentences.zh: 間數年，烏春來攻，世祖拒之。

translations.literal: After several years Wuchun came to attack, and the World Ancestor resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later Wuchun attacked, and the World Ancestor met him in arms.

sentences.zh: 時十月已半，大雨累晝夜，冰澌覆地，烏春不能進。

translations.literal: It was already mid-tenth month; heavy rain fell for days and nights, ice slush covered the ground, and Wuchun could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: It was mid-autumn; rain fell day and night until the ground was sheeted in slush ice, and Wuchun’s army could not advance.

sentences.zh: 既而悔曰：「此天也！

translations.literal: Later he repented, saying: “This is Heaven’s doing!
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun then exclaimed in regret: “This is Heaven’s will!

sentences.zh: 」乃引兵去。

translations.literal: ” He thereupon led his army away.
translations.idiomatic: ” and withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 烏春舍于阿里矮村滓不乃家，而以兵圍其弟勝昆于胡不村。

translations.literal: Wuchun lodged at Zibunai’s house in Ali’ai Village, while with his troops he besieged his younger brother Shengkun at Hubu Village.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun quartered at Zibunai’s house in Ali’ai Village while his army besieged his younger brother Shengkun at Hubu Village.

sentences.zh: 兵退，勝昆執其兄滓不乃，而請蒞殺于世祖，且請免其孥戮。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew, Shengkun seized his elder brother Zibunai and asked to bring him before the World Ancestor for execution, and also asked that his dependents be spared slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: After the retreat Shengkun seized his brother Zibunai and asked leave to bring him before the World Ancestor for execution, begging that the rest of the family be spared.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor agreed.

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達亦舉兵，遣肅宗拒之。

translations.literal: Huanran and Sandá also raised troops; he sent the Solemn Ancestor to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Huanran and Sandá also took up arms; the World Ancestor sent the Solemn Ancestor against them.

sentences.zh: 當是時，烏春兵在北，桓赧兵在南，其勢甚盛。

translations.literal: At that time Wuchun’s army was in the north and Huanran’s in the south; their power was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun threatened from the north and Huanran from the south; their combined strength was formidable.

sentences.zh: 戒之曰：「可和則與之和，否則決戰！

translations.literal: He admonished him: “Make peace if you can; otherwise fight to the decision!
translations.idiomatic: He instructed him: “Treat for peace if possible; otherwise fight it out!

sentences.zh: 」肅宗兵敗。

translations.literal: ” The Solemn Ancestor’s army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Solemn Ancestor was defeated.

sentences.zh: 會烏春以久雨解去，世祖乃以偏師涉舍很水，經貼割水，覆桓赧、散達之家。

translations.literal: When Wuchun withdrew on account of the long rains, the World Ancestor with a detached force crossed the Shehan River, passed the Tiege River, and overran the homes of Huanran and Sandá.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchun withdrew in the rains, the World Ancestor led a detachment across the Shehan and Tiege rivers and ravaged the homes of Huanran and Sandá.

sentences.zh: 明日，大霧晦冥，失道，至婆多吐水乃覺。

translations.literal: The next day a great fog darkened the sky; they lost their way and only realized it when they reached the Potuotuo River.
translations.idiomatic: The next day a dense fog blinded them; they lost their way and only found their bearings at the Potuotuo River.

sentences.zh: 即還至舍很、貼割之間，升高阜望之，見六騎來，大呼，馳擊之。

translations.literal: Returning between Shehan and Tiege, they climbed a high knoll to look about and saw six horsemen coming; they shouted and charged to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Marching back between the Shehan and Tiege, they climbed a height and sighted six horsemen; they shouted and galloped to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 世祖射一人斃，生獲五人，問之，乃知卜灰、撒骨出使助恆赧、散達者也。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor shot one dead, captured five alive, and questioned them; he learned they were Buhui and Saguchu, sent to aid Huanran and Sandá.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor shot one dead and took five alive; they proved to be Buhui and Saguchu, envoys sent to assist Huanran and Sandá.

sentences.zh: 世祖至桓赧、散達所居，焚蕩其室家。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor reached the dwellings of Huanran and Sandá and burned and destroyed their houses.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the settlements of Huanran and Sandá and burned them to the ground.

sentences.zh: 殺百許人，舊將主保亦死之。

translations.literal: He killed about a hundred men; the old chief Zhuba also died in this.
translations.idiomatic: About a hundred men were killed, including the veteran chief Zhuba.

sentences.zh: 比世祖還，與肅宗會，肅宗兵又敗矣。

translations.literal: When the World Ancestor returned and met the Solemn Ancestor, the Solemn Ancestor’s army had again been defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he joined the Solemn Ancestor—only to learn that his army had been beaten again.

sentences.zh: 世祖讓肅宗失利之狀。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor reproached the Solemn Ancestor for his defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor rebuked the Solemn Ancestor for the loss.

sentences.zh: 遣人議和，桓赧、散達曰：「以爾盈歌之大赤馬、辭不失之紫騮馬與我，我則和。

translations.literal: He sent men to negotiate peace; Huanran and Sandá said: “Give us Yingge’s great red horse and Cibushi’s purple bay, and we will make peace.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to treat for peace; Huanran and Sandá demanded: “Give us Yingge’s great red stallion and Cibushi’s purple bay, and we will make peace.

sentences.zh: 」二馬皆女直名馬，不許。

translations.literal: ” Both horses were famed Jurchen steeds; he would not grant them.
translations.idiomatic: ” Both were famed Jurchen horses; the World Ancestor refused.

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達大會諸部來攻，過裴滿部，以其附于世祖也，縱火焚之。

translations.literal: Huanran and Sandá assembled the tribes to attack; passing the Puman tribe, because it had submitted to the World Ancestor they set fire and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: Huanran and Sandá mustered the tribes and marched; passing the Puman tribe, which had sided with the World Ancestor, they put it to the torch.

sentences.zh: 蒲察部沙祇勃堇、胡補答勃堇使阿喜來告難，世祖使之詭從以自全，曰：「戰則以旗鼓自別。

translations.literal: Shazhi, chief of the Pucha tribe, and Hubuda, chief of the Hupuda tribe, sent Axi to report their distress; the World Ancestor had him pretend submission to preserve himself, saying: “In battle, distinguish yourselves by flags and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs Shazhi of the Pucha and Hubuda of the Hupuda sent Axi to plead for help; the World Ancestor bade him feign compliance to survive, saying: “In the fight, mark yourselves by flags and drums.

sentences.zh: 」世祖往禦桓赧之衆，將行，有報者曰：「跋黑食於愛妾之父家，肉脹咽死矣！

translations.literal: ” As the World Ancestor was about to go forth against Huanran’s host, a messenger reported: “Bahei, dining at his favorite concubine’s father’s house, choked to death on swollen meat!
translations.idiomatic: ” As he prepared to meet Huanran’s army, word came: “Bahei, feasting at his concubine’s father’s house, has choked to death on a swelling in his throat!

sentences.zh: 」乃遣肅宗求援於遼，遂率衆出。

translations.literal: ” He then sent the Solemn Ancestor to seek aid from the Liao and led his army out.
translations.idiomatic: ” He dispatched the Solemn Ancestor to seek Liao aid and took the field.

sentences.zh: 使辭不失取海姑兄弟兵，已而乃知海姑兄弟貳於桓赧矣。

translations.literal: He had Cibushi fetch the Haigu brothers’ troops, but soon learned the Haigu brothers had turned to Huanran.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Cibushi to bring the Haigu brothers’ warriors, only to learn they had already gone over to Huanran.

sentences.zh: 欲並取其衆，徑至海姑。

translations.literal: He wished to seize their forces as well and went straight to Haigu.
translations.idiomatic: Intending to seize their forces as well, he marched straight for Haigu.

sentences.zh: 偵者報曰：「敵已至。

translations.literal: Scouts reported: “The enemy has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported: “The enemy is upon us.

sentences.zh: 」將戰，世祖戒辭不失曰：「汝先陣於脫豁改原，待吾三揚旗，三鳴鼓，即棄旗決戰。

translations.literal: ” About to give battle, the World Ancestor charged Cibushi: “Take the vanguard at Tuohuogai Plain; wait until I raise the banner three times and beat the drum three times, then cast down the banner and join the fight.
translations.idiomatic: ” Before the clash he charged Cibushi: “Hold the van at Tuohuogai Plain; when I raise my banner thrice and sound the drum thrice, cast down your banner and charge.

sentences.zh: 死生惟在今日，命不足惜！

translations.literal: Life and death hang on this day; do not spare your lives!
translations.idiomatic: Life or death turns on this day—hold nothing back!

sentences.zh: 」使裴滿胡喜牽大紫騮馬以爲貳馬，馳至陣。

translations.literal: ” He had the Puman Hu Xi lead the great purple bay as a spare mount and galloped to the line.
translations.idiomatic: ” He had the Puman Hu Xi lead the great purple bay as a reserve mount and rode to the front.

sentences.zh: 時桓赧、散達盛強，世祖軍吏未戰而懼，皆植立無人色。

translations.literal: Huanran and Sandá were at the height of their power; the World Ancestor’s officers had not yet fought and were already afraid, standing rooted and colorless.
translations.idiomatic: Huanran and Sandá were at the zenith of their strength; the World Ancestor’s officers had not yet crossed spears and already stood pale and rigid with fear.

sentences.zh: 世祖陽陽如平常，亦無責讓之言，但令士卒解甲少憩，以水沃面，調蒨水飲之。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor appeared as calm as on any ordinary day and uttered no word of reproach, only ordering the soldiers to remove their armor and rest a little, wash their faces with water, and drink diluted madder water.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor seemed as serene as on any ordinary day and spoke no rebuke, only bidding the men doff their armor, rest briefly, wash their faces, and drink diluted madder water.

sentences.zh: 有頃，訓勵之，軍勢復振。

translations.literal: After a while he exhorted them, and army morale revived.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he rallied them, and their spirit returned.

sentences.zh: 乃避衆獨引穆宗，執其手密與之言曰：「今日之事，若勝則已，萬一有不勝，吾必無生。

translations.literal: He then drew the Mournful Ancestor aside from the host, took his hand, and spoke to him in secret: “If today’s affair succeeds, well and good; if by any chance we do not prevail, I shall surely not survive.
translations.idiomatic: He drew the Mournful Ancestor apart, took his hand, and whispered: “If we win today, all is well; if we should lose, I will not live.

sentences.zh: 汝今介馬遙觀，勿預戰事。

translations.literal: You now, on a separate horse, watch from afar and do not join the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Take a horse apart and watch from a distance—do not enter the fight.

sentences.zh: 若我死，汝勿收吾骨，勿顧戀親戚，亟馳馬奔告汝兄頗剌淑，於遼系籍受印，乞師以報此仇！

translations.literal: If I die, do not gather my bones, do not linger over kin; ride swiftly and tell your brother Pilashi to enter Liao registers, accept the seal, and beg troops to avenge this wrong!
translations.idiomatic: If I fall, do not collect my bones or tarry for kin—ride at once to your brother Pilashi, enter the Liao registers, accept their seal, and beg an army to avenge this defeat!

sentences.zh: 」語畢，袒袖，不被甲，以縕袍垂襴護前後心，韔弓提劍，三揚旗，三鳴鼓，棄旗搏戰，身爲軍鋒，突入敵陣，衆從之。

translations.literal: ” When he had finished speaking, he bared his arms, wore no armor, protected his breast before and behind with a padded robe whose skirt hung down, slung his bow and grasped his sword, raised the banner three times, beat the drum three times, cast down the banner and grappled in battle, himself leading the army’s point and plunging into the enemy ranks, and the host followed.
translations.idiomatic: ” He bared his arms, wore no armor, shielded his chest with a padded robe, slung his bow and drew his sword, thrice raised his banner, thrice sounded the drum, cast the banner down and charged at the head of the army into the enemy line, and his warriors followed.

sentences.zh: 辭不失從後奮擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Cibushi struck from the rear and they were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Cibushi fell upon them from behind, and the enemy was utterly routed.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐之，自阿不彎至於北隘甸，死者如僕麻，破多吐水水爲之赤，棄車甲馬牛軍實盡獲之。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory in pursuit, from Abuwan to Beiai Plain, the dead lay thick as fallen hemp stalks; at Poduo Tushui the water was turned red, and abandoned carts, armor, horses, oxen, and all military stores were wholly captured.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the rout from Abuwan to Beiai Plain, where corpses piled like cut hemp; at Poduo Tushui the stream ran red, and every abandoned cart, suit of armor, horse, ox, and store of war booty fell into their hands.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「今日之捷，非天不能及此，亦可以知足矣。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor said: “Today’s victory—without Heaven it could not have reached this; we may also know when to be satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor said: “This day’s triumph could not have come but for Heaven; we have reason enough to be content.

sentences.zh: 雖縱之去，敗軍之氣，沒世不振。

translations.literal: Even if we let them go, the spirit of a defeated army will not revive in a lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: Even were we to let them escape, a broken army would never rise again in their lifetimes.

sentences.zh: 」乃引軍還。

translations.literal: ” He then led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: ” With that he withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 世祖視其戰地，馳突成大路，闊且三十隴。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor surveyed the battlefield; the charges and clashes had worn a great road, broad enough for some thirty ridges.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor looked over the field of battle, where repeated charges had trampled a broad track some thirty ridges wide.

sentences.zh: 手殺九人，自相重積，人皆異之。

translations.literal: With his own hand he had killed nine men, piled one upon another; all marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: He had personally slain nine men, their bodies heaped together—a feat that astonished all who saw it.

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達自此不能復聚，未幾，各以其屬來降，遼大安七年也。

translations.literal: Huanran and Sandá from this time could no longer gather again; before long each came to submit with his followers—it was the seventh year of Liao Da’an.
translations.idiomatic: Huanran and Sandá never again mustered their strength; within a short time each surrendered with his followers, in the seventh year of Liao Da’an.

sentences.zh: 初，桓赧兄弟之變，不术魯部卜灰、蒲察部撒骨出助之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huanran and his brothers rebelled, Buhui of the Bushilu tribe and Saguchu of the Pucha tribe had aided them.
translations.idiomatic: When Huanran and his brothers had first risen, Buhui of the Bushilu tribe and Saguchu of the Pucha tribe had supported them.

sentences.zh: 至是，招之，不肯和。

translations.literal: At this time they were summoned, but refused to make peace.
translations.idiomatic: Now they were called to submit, but would not accept peace.

sentences.zh: 卜灰之党石魯遂殺卜灰來降。

translations.literal: Shilu, a follower of Buhui, then killed Buhui and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu, one of Buhui’s partisans, slew Buhui and came over in submission.

sentences.zh: 撒骨出追躡亡者，道傍人潛射之，中口而死。

translations.literal: Saguchu pursued the fugitives; a man by the roadside shot him in secret, striking his mouth, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Saguchu gave chase to the fugitives; someone hidden by the road shot him through the mouth, and he fell dead.

sentences.zh: 自是舊部悉歸。

translations.literal: From this time all the old followers wholly returned.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every former follower came back into the fold.

sentences.zh: 景祖時，斡勒部人杯乃來屬，及是，有他志。

translations.literal: In the time of the Accomplished Ancestor, Beinai of the Wanyan tribe had come to submit; now he harbored other designs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Accomplished Ancestor’s day Beinai of the Wanyan tribe had submitted; now he turned disloyal.

sentences.zh: 會其家失火，因以縱火誣歡部，世祖征償如約。

translations.literal: When his house caught fire, he used the arson to accuse the Huan tribe; the World Ancestor marched to exact compensation as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: After fire broke out at his home, he blamed the Huan tribe for setting it; the World Ancestor marched to collect the indemnity owed by custom.

sentences.zh: 杯乃不自安，遂結烏春、窩謀罕舉兵。

translations.literal: Beinai grew uneasy and thereupon joined Wuchun and Womouhan in raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: Beinai, ill at ease, allied with Wuchun and Womouhan and took up arms.

sentences.zh: 使肅宗與戰，敗之，獲杯乃，世祖獻之於遼。

translations.literal: He sent the Solemn Ancestor to fight them, defeated them, captured Beinai, and the World Ancestor presented him to the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched the Solemn Ancestor against them, routed them, seized Beinai, and the World Ancestor delivered him to the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 臘醅、麻產侵掠野居女直，略來流水牧馬。

translations.literal: Lapei and Machan raided the wild Jurchen and drove off horses pastured at Laishui River.
translations.idiomatic: Lapei and Machan plundered the wild Jurchen and carried off horses grazing along Laishui River.

sentences.zh: 世祖擊之，中四創，久之疾愈。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor struck them, received four wounds, and after a long time his illness healed.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor attacked them, took four wounds, and only after a long convalescence recovered.

sentences.zh: 臘醅等復略穆宗牧馬，交結諸部。

translations.literal: Lapei and the others again drove off the Mournful Ancestor’s horses and allied with various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Lapei and his allies again rustled the Mournful Ancestor’s horses and won over other tribes.

sentences.zh: 世祖復伐之，臘醅等紿降，乃旋。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor again campaigned against them; Lapei and the others feigned surrender, and he then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor marched against them again; Lapei and his men pretended to submit, and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 臘醅得姑里甸兵百十有七人，據暮稜水守險，石顯子婆諸刊亦在其中。

translations.literal: Lapei mustered one hundred seventeen soldiers from Guli-dian, held the defiles along the Muleng River, and Shi Xian’s son Pozhukan was also among them.
translations.idiomatic: Lapei gathered one hundred seventeen warriors from Guli-dian, seized the heights at Muleng River, and Shi Xian’s son Pozhukan was in their ranks.

sentences.zh: 世祖圍而克之，盡獲姑里甸兵。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor besieged and took them, capturing all the Guli-dian soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor invested the position, broke it, and took every Guli-dian fighter captive.

sentences.zh: 麻產遁去。

translations.literal: Machan fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Machan escaped.

sentences.zh: 遂擒臘醅及婆諸刊，皆獻之遼。

translations.literal: He then seized Lapei and Pozhukan and presented them both to the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured Lapei and Pozhukan and sent them both to the Liao as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 既已，復請之，遼人與之，並以前後所獻罪人歸之。

translations.literal: Afterward he again requested them; the Liao people returned them, together with the criminals previously presented on earlier occasions.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked the Liao to return them; the Liao complied, sending back these men along with every offender previously delivered to them.

sentences.zh: 歡都在破烏春等於斜堆，故石、拔石皆就擒。

translations.literal: Huandu, in defeating Wuchun and the others at Xiedui, thereby captured Gu Shi and Ba Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Huandu’s victory over Wuchun and his allies at Xiedui also brought Gu Shi and Ba Shi into captivity.

sentences.zh: 世祖自將與歡都合兵嶺東，諸軍皆至。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor personally led the army to join Huandu east of the pass; all the forces arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor took command in person and united with Huandu east of the ridge; every contingent came up.

sentences.zh: 是時，烏春已前死，窩謀罕請於遼，願和解。

translations.literal: At this time Wuchun had already died earlier; Womouhan petitioned the Liao, wishing to make peace.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wuchun was already dead; Womouhan appealed to the Liao, seeking reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 既與和，復來襲，乃進軍圍之。

translations.literal: Once peace had been made, he again came to raid; the army therefore advanced and besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had peace been settled when he struck again; the Jurchen army marched forward and laid siege to him.

sentences.zh: 窩謀罕棄城遁去。

translations.literal: Womouhan abandoned the city and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Womouhan deserted the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 破其城，盡俘獲之，以功差次分賜諸軍。

translations.literal: They broke his city, captured all within, and distributed rewards to the armies according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the city, took everyone captive, and divided the spoils among the troops by rank of service.

sentences.zh: 城始破，議渠長生殺，衆皆長跪，遼使者在坐。

translations.literal: When the city was first taken, they debated whether to execute the chieftain; all knelt in a long line, and a Liao envoy sat present.
translations.idiomatic: As the city fell, they debated putting the chieftain to death; the whole assembly knelt in ranks while a Liao envoy looked on.

sentences.zh: 忽一人佩長刀突前咫尺，謂世祖曰：「勿殺我！

translations.literal: Suddenly one man, wearing a long sword, rushed forward to within a foot and said to the World Ancestor: “Do not kill me!
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a man with a long sword at his belt burst forward to arm’s length and cried to the World Ancestor: “Spare my life!

sentences.zh: 」遼使及左右皆走匿。

translations.literal: ” The Liao envoy and those at the World Ancestor’s side all fled and hid.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Liao envoy and the World Ancestor’s attendants scattered in panic.

sentences.zh: 世祖色不少動，執其人之手，語之曰：「吾不殺汝也。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor’s countenance did not change in the least; he took the man’s hand and said to him: “I will not kill you.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor did not so much as flinch; he seized the man’s hand and said: “I will not take your life.

sentences.zh: 」於是罰左右匿者，曰：「汝等何敢失次耶？

translations.literal: ” He then punished those at his side who had hidden themselves, saying: “How dare you break ranks?
translations.idiomatic: ” He then punished the attendants who had fled, saying: “How dare you abandon your posts?

sentences.zh: 」罰既已，乃徐使執突前者殺之。

translations.literal: ” When the punishment was finished, he then slowly had the man who had rushed forward seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Once discipline had been restored, he calmly ordered the intruder taken and executed.

sentences.zh: 其膽勇鎮物如此。

translations.literal: His courage and composure in quelling others were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the steadiness with which his courage imposed order on those around him.

sentences.zh: 師還，寢疾，遂篤。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he took to his bed with illness and soon grew gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: On the homeward march he fell bedridden; his illness swiftly turned grave.

sentences.zh: 元娶拏懶氏哭不止，世祖曰：「汝勿哭，汝惟後我一歲耳。

translations.literal: His primary consort of the Nalan clan wept without cease; the World Ancestor said: “Do not weep—you will follow me by only one year.
translations.idiomatic: His chief wife of the Nalan clan would not stop weeping; the World Ancestor said: “Weep no more—you will outlive me by only one year.

sentences.zh: 」肅宗請後事，曰：「汝惟後我三年。

translations.literal: ” The Solemn Ancestor asked about affairs after his death; he said: “You will follow me by only three years.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Solemn Ancestor asked what lay ahead; he answered: “You will outlive me by only three years.

sentences.zh: 」肅宗出，謂人曰：「吾兄至此，亦不與我好言。

translations.literal: ” When the Solemn Ancestor went out, he said to others: “My elder brother, even at this point, will not speak kindly to me.
translations.idiomatic: ” Leaving the chamber, the Solemn Ancestor told others: “Even now my brother will not grant me a kind word.

sentences.zh: 」乃叩地而哭。

translations.literal: ” He then beat his head upon the ground and wept.
translations.idiomatic: ” Then he bowed his head to the earth and wept.

sentences.zh: 俄呼穆宗謂曰：「烏雅束柔善，若辦集契丹事，阿骨打能之。

translations.literal: Soon he summoned the Mournful Ancestor and said: “Wuyashu is gentle and good; if one must manage Khitan affairs, Aguda is equal to the task.
translations.idiomatic: He soon called for the Mournful Ancestor and said: “Wuyashu is mild and trustworthy; when Khitan business must be handled, Aguda can manage it.

sentences.zh: 」遼大安八年五月十五日卒。

translations.literal: ” On the fifteenth day of the fifth month of the eighth year of Liao Da’an he died.
translations.idiomatic: ” He died on the fifteenth day of the fifth month in the eighth year of Liao Da’an.

sentences.zh: 襲位十九年，年五十四。

translations.literal: He had held the succession nineteen years and was fifty-four years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He had ruled nineteen years and was fifty-four at his death.

sentences.zh: 明年，拏懶氏卒。

translations.literal: The next year the Lady of the Nalan clan died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Nalan consort died.

sentences.zh: 又明年，肅宗卒。

translations.literal: The year after that the Solemn Ancestor died.
translations.idiomatic: In the next year the Solemn Ancestor too passed away.

sentences.zh: 肅宗病篤，歎曰：「我兄真多智哉！

translations.literal: When the Solemn Ancestor lay gravely ill, he sighed and said: “My elder brother was truly full of wisdom!
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed the Solemn Ancestor sighed: “My brother was farseeing indeed!

sentences.zh: 」世祖天性嚴重，有智識，一見必識，暫聞不忘。

translations.literal: ” By nature the World Ancestor was stern and grave, possessed of wisdom and discernment; what he saw once he always recognized, and what he heard briefly he did not forget.
translations.idiomatic: ” The World Ancestor was by nature austere and weighty, keen of mind; faces seen once he never forgot, and words heard in passing he retained.

sentences.zh: 凝寒不縮栗，動止不回顧。

translations.literal: In bitter cold he did not shiver; in movement and rest he did not look back.
translations.idiomatic: He did not tremble in freezing cold, and he never glanced over his shoulder as he moved.

sentences.zh: 每戰未嘗被甲，先以夢兆候其勝負。

translations.literal: In every battle he never wore armor, first using dream omens to foretell victory or defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He never donned armor in battle, trusting first to dream-omens for victory or defeat.

sentences.zh: 嘗乘醉騎驢入室中，明日見驢足跡，問而知之，自是不復飲酒。

translations.literal: Once, drunk, he rode a donkey into the house; the next day, seeing the donkey’s tracks, he inquired and learned of it, and from then on drank no more wine.
translations.idiomatic: Once, in his cups, he rode a donkey indoors; finding its tracks the next morning, he questioned his household, learned what he had done, and never drank again.

sentences.zh: 襲位之初，內外潰叛，締交爲寇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of his succession, within and without there were collapse and rebellion, and alliances turned to enmity.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took power, rebellion erupted at home and abroad, and former allies became foes.

sentences.zh: 世祖乃因敗爲功，變弱爲強。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor then turned defeat into achievement and weakness into strength.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor turned reverses into triumph and weakness into power.

sentences.zh: 既破桓赧、散達、烏春、窩謀罕，基業自此大矣。

translations.literal: Once he had broken Huanran, Sandá, Wuchun, and Womouhan, the foundation of the enterprise from this time became great.
translations.idiomatic: After breaking Huanran, Sandá, Wuchun, and Womouhan, the house’s foundation was secure and its power greatly enlarged.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，追諡聖肅皇帝，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously titled Emperor Shengsu, with the temple name Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he received the posthumous title Emperor Shengsu and the temple name Shizu.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏曰永陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named Yong Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong his tomb was designated Yong Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡世祖神武聖肅皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his posthumous title was augmented to World Ancestor Emperor Shenwu Shengsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was expanded to World Ancestor Emperor Shenwu Shengsu.

sentences.zh: 母弟頗剌淑襲節度使，景祖第四子也，是爲肅宗。

translations.literal: His younger uterine brother Pilashi succeeded to the military commissionership; he was the fourth son of the Accomplished Ancestor—this was the Solemn Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother by the same mother, Pilashi, inherited the military commissionership; the Accomplished Ancestor’s fourth son, he is known as the Solemn Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 遼重熙十一年壬午歲生。

translations.literal: He was born in the renwu year, the eleventh year of Liao Chongxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the renwu year of the eleventh year of Liao Chongxi (1042).

sentences.zh: 在父兄時號國相。

translations.literal: In the time of his father and elder brothers he was called State Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: While his father and elder brothers still ruled, he was known as State Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 國相之稱不知始何時。

translations.literal: When the title State Chancellor began is not known.
translations.idiomatic: When the office of State Chancellor originated is unknown.

sentences.zh: 初，雅達爲國相。

translations.literal: At first Yada served as State Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Yada had been State Chancellor before him.

sentences.zh: 雅達者，桓赧、散達之父也。

translations.literal: Yada was the father of Huanran and Sandá.
translations.idiomatic: Yada was Huanran and Sandá’s father.

sentences.zh: 景祖以幣馬求之于雅達，而命肅宗爲之。

translations.literal: The Accomplished Ancestor sought him from Yada with gifts of silks and horses, and appointed the Solemn Ancestor to the office.
translations.idiomatic: The Accomplished Ancestor exchanged silks and horses with Yada for the post and installed the Solemn Ancestor as State Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 肅宗自幼機敏善辯。

translations.literal: The Solemn Ancestor from youth was quick-witted and skilled in debate.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood the Solemn Ancestor was sharp and eloquent.

sentences.zh: 當其兄時，身居國相，盡心匡輔。

translations.literal: While his elder brother ruled, he held the office of State Chancellor and devoted himself wholly to support and aid.
translations.idiomatic: During his elder brother’s reign he served as State Chancellor and gave himself entirely to counsel and support.

sentences.zh: 是時，叔父跋黑有異志，及桓赧、散達、烏春、窩謀罕、石顯父子、臘醅、麻產作難，用兵之際，肅宗屢當一面。

translations.literal: At that time his uncle Bahei harbored divergent ambitions; when Huanran, Sandá, Wuchun, Womouhan, Shi Xian and his son, Lapei, and Machan raised trouble, in the midst of campaigning the Solemn Ancestor repeatedly held one front alone.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Bahei then nursed rebellious designs; when Huanran, Sandá, Wuchun, Womouhan, Shi Xian and his son, Lapei, and Machan rose in revolt, the Solemn Ancestor repeatedly commanded a wing of the army by himself.

sentences.zh: 尤能知遼人國政人情。

translations.literal: He was especially able to understand Liao statecraft and human sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Above all he understood Liao politics and the temper of its people.

sentences.zh: 凡有遼事，一切委之肅宗專心焉。
