translations.literal: Whenever there was a Liao matter, everything was entrusted to the Solemn Ancestor with full attention.
translations.idiomatic: Every affair touching the Liao was entrusted entirely to the Solemn Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 凡白事於遼官，皆令遠跪陳辭，譯者傳致之，往往爲譯者錯亂。

translations.literal: Whenever one reported business to Liao officials, all were made to kneel at a distance and state their case; interpreters transmitted it, and often the interpreters garbled the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Petitioners before Liao officials were required to kneel far off and speak through interpreters, who often mangled what was said.

sentences.zh: 肅宗欲得自前委曲言之，故先不以實告譯者。

translations.literal: The Solemn Ancestor wished to come forward himself and explain the details; therefore he first did not tell the interpreters the full truth.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to speak for himself in full detail, the Solemn Ancestor deliberately withheld the facts from the interpreters.

sentences.zh: 譯者惑之，不得已，引之前，使自言。

translations.literal: The interpreters were perplexed; having no choice, they led him forward and had him speak for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Baffled, the interpreters at last brought him forward and let him address the court directly.

sentences.zh: 乃以草木瓦石爲籌，枚數其事而陳之。

translations.literal: He then took grass, wood, tiles, and stones as counters and, counting them off item by item, set forth the matters.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out stalks, pebbles, and shards as counters and, tallying each point in turn, stated his case.

sentences.zh: 官吏聽者皆愕然，問其故，則爲卑辭以對曰：「鄙陋無文，故如此。

translations.literal: The officials who listened were all astonished; asked the reason, he answered with humble words: “I am crude and without learning, therefore it is like this.
translations.idiomatic: The officials stared in amazement; when they asked why, he answered humbly: “I am unlettered and rough, and so must speak in this way.

sentences.zh: 」官吏以爲實然，不復疑之，是以所訴無不如意。

translations.literal: ” The officials thought it genuine and no longer doubted him; thus in every petition there was nothing that did not go as he wished.
translations.idiomatic: ” Taking this for sincerity, they ceased to suspect him, and thereafter every plea he brought won its desired outcome.

sentences.zh: 桓赧、散達之戰，部人賽罕死之，其弟活羅陰懷忿怨。

translations.literal: In the war with Huanran and Sandá, a tribesman named Saihan died; his younger brother Huoluo secretly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Huanran and Sandá, the tribesman Saihan was killed; his younger brother Huoluo nursed a private grudge.

sentences.zh: 一日，忽以劍脊置肅宗項上曰：「吾兄爲汝輩死矣！

translations.literal: One day he suddenly placed the back of his sword upon the Solemn Ancestor’s neck and said: “My elder brother died for you people!
translations.idiomatic: One day he set the flat of his blade against the Solemn Ancestor’s neck and cried: “My brother died for your sake!

sentences.zh: 剄汝以償，則如之何？

translations.literal: If I cut your throat to repay it, what then?
translations.idiomatic: If I slit your throat in payment, what of it?

sentences.zh: 」久之，因其兄柩至，遂怒而攻習不出，習不出走避之。

translations.literal: ” After a long while, because his elder brother’s coffin arrived, he then in anger attacked Xi Buchu; Xi Buchu fled to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Some time later, when his brother’s bier arrived, he flew into a rage and attacked Xi Buchu, who fled to escape him.

sentences.zh: 攻肅宗於家，矢注次室之裙，著於門扉。

translations.literal: He attacked the Solemn Ancestor at home; an arrow pierced the skirt of the side chamber and lodged in the door panel.
translations.idiomatic: He assaulted the Solemn Ancestor’s house; one arrow pinned the hem of an inner room’s curtain to the doorframe.

sentences.zh: 復攻歡都，歡都衷甲拒於室中，既不能入，持其門旃而去，往附杯乃。

translations.literal: He again attacked Huandu; Huandu wore armor beneath his robes and barred the door from within; unable to enter, he seized the door banner and departed, going to join Beinai.
translations.idiomatic: He next attacked Huandu, who armored himself and held the room; failing to break in, he tore down the door banner and went over to Beinai.

sentences.zh: 杯乃誘烏春兵度嶺，世祖與遇于蘇素海甸。

translations.literal: Beinai lured Wuchun’s troops across the pass; the World Ancestor met them at Sushuhai Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Beinai drew Wuchun’s army over the ridge; the World Ancestor intercepted them at Sushuhai Plain.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「予昔有異夢，今不可親戰。

translations.literal: The World Ancestor said: “I once had an unusual dream; today I cannot fight in person.
translations.idiomatic: The World Ancestor said: “I once had an ominous dream; today I must not enter the fight myself.

sentences.zh: 若左軍中有力戰者，則大功成矣！

translations.literal: If among the left army there is one who fights with force, then the great achievement will be accomplished!
translations.idiomatic: If someone on the left wing fights with all his strength, the day will be ours!

sentences.zh: 」命肅宗及斜列、辭不失與之戰。

translations.literal: ” He ordered the Solemn Ancestor, Xielie, and Cibushi to engage them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent the Solemn Ancestor, Xielie, and Cibushi to give battle.

sentences.zh: 肅宗下馬，名呼世祖，復自呼其名而言曰：「若天助我當爲衆部長，則今日之事神祇監之。

translations.literal: The Solemn Ancestor dismounted, called the World Ancestor by name, then called his own name and said: “If Heaven helps me to become chief of all the tribes, then let the spirits witness today’s affair.
translations.idiomatic: The Solemn Ancestor dismounted, invoked the World Ancestor by name, then his own, and declared: “If Heaven intends me as chief of all the tribes, let the spirits witness this day.

sentences.zh: 」語畢再拜。

translations.literal: ” When he had finished speaking he bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: ” Having spoken, he bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 遂炷火束縕。

translations.literal: He then lit fire to a bundle of kindling.
translations.idiomatic: He then set a bundle of kindling ablaze.

sentences.zh: 頃之，大風自後起，火益熾。

translations.literal: Before long a great wind rose from behind, and the fire burned all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a strong wind rose at their backs and the flames leapt higher.

sentences.zh: 是時八月，並青草皆焚之，煙焰漲天。

translations.literal: It was then the eighth month, and even the green grass was all burned; smoke and flame filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: It was the eighth month; the blaze consumed even the green grass, and smoke and fire blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 我軍隨煙衝擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Our army followed the smoke in a charge and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen army charged through the smoke and routed the enemy completely.

sentences.zh: 遂獲杯乃，囚而獻諸遼。

translations.literal: They then captured Beinai, imprisoned him, and presented him to the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Beinai, bound him, and delivered him to the Liao.

sentences.zh: 並獲活羅，肅宗釋其罪，左右任使之，後竟得其力焉。

translations.literal: Huoluo was also captured; the Solemn Ancestor pardoned his crime and kept him at his side to employ as he wished, and in the end he indeed proved useful.
translations.idiomatic: Huoluo was taken as well; the Solemn Ancestor forgave him, kept him close, and put him to use—and in time he repaid the trust.

sentences.zh: 大安八年，自國相襲位。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Da’an he succeeded from the office of State Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Da’an he succeeded to rule from the post of State Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 是時，麻產尚據直屋鎧水，繕完營堡，誘納亡命。

translations.literal: At that time Machan still held Zhiwu Kai River, repaired and completed his camps and fortresses, and enticed and received fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Machan still held Zhiwu Kai River, rebuilt his camps and strongholds, and welcomed runaways to his banner.

sentences.zh: 招之，不聽，遣康宗伐之。

translations.literal: They summoned him, but he would not listen; they dispatched Kang Zong to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned he refused submission; Kang Zong was sent to attack him.

sentences.zh: 太祖別軍取麻產家屬，錡釜無遺。

translations.literal: Taizu with a separate army took Machan’s dependents, leaving not even a cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu led a detached force against Machan’s household and stripped it bare, not a pot left behind.

sentences.zh: 既獲麻產，殺之，獻馘於遼。

translations.literal: Once Machan had been captured, they killed him and presented his head to the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Machan was taken and executed, and his head was sent to the Liao as tribute.

sentences.zh: 陶溫水民來附。

translations.literal: The people of the Taowen River came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Taowen River tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 二年癸酉，遣太祖以偏師伐泥厖古部帥水抹離海村跋黑、播立開，平之，自是寇賊皆息。

translations.literal: In the second year, guiyou, he dispatched Taizu with a detached force to campaign against Baghei and Bolikai, chiefs of the Nimogugu tribe at Shuimoli Haicun, and pacified them; from this time banditry ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1093), Taizu was sent with a detached column against Baghei and Bolikai, chiefs of the Nimogugu at Shuimoli Haicun; both were subdued, and raiding ceased thereafter.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，肅宗卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, the Solemn Ancestor died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year the Solemn Ancestor died.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，追諡穆憲皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously titled Emperor Muxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he received the posthumous title Emperor Muxian.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，藏號泰陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named Tai Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong his tomb was designated Tai Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡肅宗明睿穆憲皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his posthumous title was augmented to Solemn Ancestor Emperor Mingrui Muxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was expanded to Solemn Ancestor Emperor Mingrui Muxian.

sentences.zh: 母弟穆宗，諱盈歌，字烏魯完，景祖第五子也。

translations.literal: His younger brother by the same mother, the Mournful Ancestor, taboo name Yingge, courtesy name Wuluwan, was the Accomplished Ancestor’s fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: His uterine younger brother, the Mournful Ancestor—whose name was Yingge and whose courtesy name was Wuluwan—was the Accomplished Ancestor’s fifth son.

sentences.zh: 南人稱揚割太師，又曰揚割追諡孝平皇帝，號穆宗，又曰揚割號仁祖。

translations.literal: Southerners call him Yangge Grand Master; they also say Yangge was posthumously titled Emperor Xiaoping and given the temple name Mournful Ancestor, and further that Yangge was styled Renzu.
translations.idiomatic: Southern sources call him Grand Master Yangge; some say Yangge received the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoping and the temple name Mournful Ancestor, and others even style him Renzu.

sentences.zh: 金代無號仁祖者，穆宗諱盈歌，諡孝平，「盈」近「揚」，「歌」近「割」，南北音訛。

translations.literal: No Jin ruler was ever titled Renzu; the Mournful Ancestor’s name was Yingge and his posthumous title Xiaoping—“Ying” approximates “Yang” and “Ge” approximates “Ge”—a corruption of northern and southern pronunciation.
translations.idiomatic: No Jin emperor ever bore the title Renzu; the Mournful Ancestor was named Yingge and posthumously titled Xiaoping—“Ying” is heard as “Yang,” “ge” as “ge”—a slip of northern and southern speech.

sentences.zh: 遼人呼節度使爲太師，自景祖至太祖皆有是稱。

translations.literal: The Liao called a military commissioner “Grand Master”; from the Accomplished Ancestor down to Taizu all bore this title.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao styled a military commissioner “Grand Master”; from the Accomplished Ancestor through Taizu, each holder of the office was so addressed.

sentences.zh: 凡《叢言》、《松漠記》、張棣《金志》等書皆無足取。

translations.literal: Such works as Congyan, Songmo Ji, and Zhang Di’s Jin Zhi are altogether unreliable.
translations.idiomatic: Books such as Congyan, Songmo Ji, and Zhang Di’s Jin Zhi are not to be trusted.

sentences.zh: 穆宗，遼重熙二十二年癸巳歲生。

translations.literal: The Mournful Ancestor was born in the guisi year, the twenty-second year of Liao Chongxi.
translations.idiomatic: The Mournful Ancestor was born in the guisi year of Liao Chongxi’s twenty-second year (1053).

sentences.zh: 肅宗時擒麻產，遼命穆宗爲詳穩。

translations.literal: When the Solemn Ancestor captured Machan, the Liao appointed the Mournful Ancestor xiangwen.
translations.idiomatic: After the Solemn Ancestor captured Machan, the Liao invested the Mournful Ancestor as xiangwen.

sentences.zh: 大安十年甲戌，襲節度使，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Da’an, jiaxu, he inherited the military commissionership, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Da’an (1094) he inherited the military commissionership, aged forty-two.

sentences.zh: 以兄劾者子撒改爲國相。

translations.literal: He made Sagai, son of his elder brother Hezhe, state minister.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Sagai, son of his elder brother Hezhe, state minister.

sentences.zh: 三年丙子，唐括部跋葛勃堇與溫都部人跋忒有舊，跋葛以事往，跋忒殺跋葛。

translations.literal: In the third year, bingzi, Bagge, chief of the Tangut tribe, had old ties with Bate of the Wendu tribe; Bagge went on a visit and Bate killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1096), Bagge, chief of the Tangut tribe, was on familiar terms with Bate of the Wendu tribe; Bagge paid a visit on business and Bate killed him.

sentences.zh: 使太祖率師伐跋忒，跋忒亡去，追及，殺之星顯水，紇石烈部阿疏、毛睹祿阻兵爲難，穆宗自將伐阿疏，撒改以偏師攻鈍恩城，拔之。

translations.literal: He sent Taizu at the head of an army against Bate; Bate fled, was pursued and killed at the Xingxian River. Ashu and Maodulu of the Heshilie tribe raised troops in rebellion; the Mournful Ancestor personally led a campaign against Ashu, while Sagai with a detached force attacked Dun’en City and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was sent against Bate; Bate fled, was overtaken, and killed at the Xingxian River. Ashu and Maodulu of the Heshilie tribe took up arms in revolt; the Mournful Ancestor marched in person against Ashu, while Sagai led a detachment against Dun’en City and captured it.

sentences.zh: 阿疏初聞來伐，乃自訴於遼。

translations.literal: When Ashu first heard they were coming, he went to plead his case before the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashu first learned of the expedition, he went to lodge his complaint with the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 遂留劾者守阿疏城，穆宗乃還。

translations.literal: He thereupon left Hezhe to hold Ashu City, and the Mournful Ancestor returned.
translations.idiomatic: He left Hezhe to hold Ashu City and the Mournful Ancestor withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會陶溫水、徒籠古水紇石烈部阿閣版及石魯阻五國鷹路，執殺遼捕鷹使者。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Hegu’ban and Shilu of the Heshilie tribe on the Taowen and Tulenggu rivers blocked the hawk route of the Five States and seized and killed a Liao hawk-capture envoy.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Hegu’ban and Shilu of the Heshilie on the Taowen and Tulenggu rivers obstructed the Five States hawk-tribute route and killed a Liao hawk-capture envoy.

sentences.zh: 遼詔穆宗討之，阿閣版等據險立柵。

translations.literal: The Liao ordered the Mournful Ancestor to punish them; Hegu’ban and the others held difficult terrain and raised palisades.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao commanded the Mournful Ancestor to suppress them; Hegu’ban and his allies fortified a strong position.

sentences.zh: 方大寒，乃募善射者操勁弓利矢攻之。

translations.literal: It was bitter cold; he therefore recruited skilled archers wielding powerful bows and sharp arrows to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In the depths of winter he recruited crack archers with heavy bows and keen arrows to storm the position.

sentences.zh: 數日，入其城，出遼使存者數人，俾之歸。

translations.literal: After several days they entered the city, freed the surviving Liao envoys, several in number, and sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the city was taken; the few surviving Liao envoys were released and sent back.

sentences.zh: 統門、渾蠢水之交烏古論部留可、詐都與蘇濱水烏古論敵庫德，起兵于米里迷石罕城，納根涅之子鈍恩亦亡去，於是兩黨作難。

translations.literal: Liu-ke and Zhadu of the Wanyan tribe at the junction of the Tongmen and Hunchun rivers, together with Dikude of the Wanyan on the Subin River, raised troops at Milimishi Han City; Dun’en, son of Nagennie, also fled—and thus the two factions made trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Liu-ke and Zhadu of the Wanyan at the Tongmen–Hunchun confluence, with Dikude of the Subin Wanyan, rose at Milimishi Han City; Dun’en, son of Nagennie, fled as well—and the two factions were at war.

sentences.zh: 八月，撒改爲都統，辭不失、阿里合懣、斡帶副之，以伐留可、詐都、塢塔等。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Sagai was made chief commander, with Cibushi, Alihemen, and Wodai as deputies, to campaign against Liu-ke, Zhadu, Wuta, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Sagai was appointed chief commander, with Cibushi, Alihemen, and Wodai as his deputies, to campaign against Liu-ke, Zhadu, Wuta, and their allies.

sentences.zh: 謾都訶、石土門伐敵庫德。

translations.literal: Manduhe and Shitumen campaigned against Dikude.
translations.idiomatic: Manduhe and Shitumen marched against Dikude.

sentences.zh: 撒改欲先平邊地城堡，或欲先取留可，莫能決，乃命太祖往。

translations.literal: Sagai wished first to pacify the border fortresses, or else first to take Liu-ke; unable to decide, he ordered Taizu to go.
translations.idiomatic: Sagai could not choose between clearing the border forts first or striking Liu-ke first; unable to decide, he sent Taizu forward.

sentences.zh: 鈍恩將援留可，乘謾都訶兵未集而攻之。

translations.literal: Dun’en was about to reinforce Liu-ke and attacked while Manduhe’s troops were not yet assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Dun’en, marching to relieve Liu-ke, struck before Manduhe’s forces had fully gathered.

sentences.zh: 石土門軍既與謾都訶會，迎擊鈍恩，大敗之，降米里迷石罕城，獲鈍恩、敵庫德，釋弗殺。

translations.literal: Shitumen’s army had already joined Manduhe and met Dun’en head-on, routing him utterly; Milimishi Han City surrendered, and Dun’en and Dikude were captured but not killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shitumen’s column joined Manduhe and met Dun’en in a head-on clash, crushing him; Milimishi Han City submitted, and Dun’en and Dikude were taken alive and spared.

sentences.zh: 太祖度盆搦嶺，與撒改會，攻破留可城，留可已先往遼矣，盡殺其城中渠長。

translations.literal: Taizu crossed Pennao Ridge, joined Sagai, and stormed Liu-ke’s city; Liu-ke had already fled to the Liao beforehand, and all the leading men in the city were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu crossed Pennao Ridge, linked up with Sagai, and stormed Liu-ke’s city; Liu-ke had already fled to the Liao, and every headman in the town was put to death.

sentences.zh: 還圍塢塔城，塢塔先已亡在外，城降於軍。

translations.literal: Returning, they besieged Wuta’s city; Wuta had already fled abroad, and the city surrendered to the army.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march they invested Wuta’s city; Wuta had already fled, and the garrison surrendered.

sentences.zh: 詐都亦降于蒲家奴，於是撫甯諸路如舊時。

translations.literal: Zhadu also surrendered to Pujianu, and thereupon the various routes were pacified as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Zhadu surrendered to Pujianu as well, and the routes were settled as before.

sentences.zh: 太師因致穆宗，教統門、渾蠢、耶悔、星顯四路及嶺東諸部自今勿復稱都部長。

translations.literal: The Grand Master thereupon reported to the Mournful Ancestor, instructing the four routes of Tongmen, Hunchun, Yehui, and Xingxian and the eastern tribes beyond the ridge that from henceforth they must no longer style themselves chiefs of the capital tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Master then reported to the Mournful Ancestor and ordered the four routes—Tongmen, Hunchun, Yehui, and Xingxian—and the eastern tribes beyond the ridge never again to call themselves chiefs of the capital tribe.

sentences.zh: 命勝官、醜阿等撫定乙離骨嶺注阿門水之西諸部居民，又命斡帶及偏裨悉平二涅囊虎、二蠢出等路寇盜而還。

translations.literal: He ordered Shengguan, Chou’a, and others to pacify the tribal peoples west of Zhua’men River at Yiligu Ridge, and also ordered Wodai and all detached commanders to thoroughly subdue banditry on the Er’nenghu and Er’chunchu routes and return.
translations.idiomatic: Shengguan, Chou’a, and others were sent to settle the tribes west of Zhua’men River at Yiligu Ridge; Wodai and the subordinate commanders were ordered to suppress brigandage on the Er’nenghu and Er’chunchu routes and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 七年庚辰，劾者尚守阿疏城，毛睹祿來降。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, gengchen, Hezhe still held Ashu City, and Maodulu came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1100) Hezhe still held Ashu City, while Maodulu came over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 阿疏猶在遼，遼使使來罷兵。

translations.literal: Ashu was still with the Liao; the Liao sent envoys to order a cease-fire.
translations.idiomatic: Ashu remained at the Liao court; the Liao dispatched envoys to halt the fighting.

sentences.zh: 未到，穆宗使烏林答石魯往佐劾者，戒之曰：「遼使來罷兵，但換我軍衣服旗幟與阿疏城中無辨，勿令遼使知之。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, the Mournful Ancestor sent Wulin’a Shilu to assist Hezhe and warned him: “When the Liao envoys come to halt the fighting, only change our army’s clothing and banners so they cannot be told apart from those in Ashu City—do not let the Liao envoys know.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoys arrived, the Mournful Ancestor sent Wulin’a Shilu to aid Hezhe with this warning: “When the Liao come to halt the siege, swap our troops’ dress and banners for those of the garrison so the envoys cannot tell friend from foe—keep them in the dark.

sentences.zh: 」因戒劾者曰：「遼使可以計卻，勿聽其言遽罷兵也。

translations.literal: ” He also warned Hezhe: “The Liao envoys can be driven off by stratagem; do not heed their words and halt the campaign in haste.
translations.idiomatic: ” He also told Hezhe: “The Liao envoys can be turned back by a ruse—do not listen to them and break off the attack.

sentences.zh: 」遼使果來罷兵，穆宗使蒲察部胡魯勃堇、邈遜孛堇與俱至阿疏城。

translations.literal: ” The Liao envoys did come to halt the fighting; the Mournful Ancestor sent Chief Hulu of the Pucha tribe and Chief Miaosun, who proceeded with them to Ashu City.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Liao envoys duly arrived to stop the fighting; the Mournful Ancestor sent Chief Hulu of the Pucha tribe and Chief Miaosun to accompany them to Ashu City.

sentences.zh: 劾者見遼使，詭謂胡魯、邈遜曰：「我部族自相攻擊，幹汝等何事？

translations.literal: When Hezhe saw the Liao envoys, he deceptively said to Hulu and Miaosun: “Our tribes are fighting among ourselves—what business is it of yours?
translations.idiomatic: When Hezhe met the Liao envoys, he feigned outrage before Hulu and Miaosun: “Our clans are at war among ourselves—what is that to you?

sentences.zh: 誰識汝之太師？

translations.literal: Who recognizes your Grand Master?
translations.idiomatic: Who ever heard of your Grand Master?

sentences.zh: 」乃援創刺殺胡魯、邈遜所乘馬。

translations.literal: ” He then drew a blade and stabbed the horses ridden by Hulu and Miaosun.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then drew a knife and stabbed the horses Hulu and Miaosun were riding.

sentences.zh: 遼使驚駭遽走，不敢回顧，徑歸。

translations.literal: The Liao envoys were terrified and fled at once, not daring to look back, and went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao envoys fled in terror without a backward glance and rode straight home.

sentences.zh: 居數日，破其城。

translations.literal: After several days they stormed the city.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the city was taken by storm.

sentences.zh: 狄故保還自遼。

translations.literal: Di Gubao returned from the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Di Gubao returned from the Liao.

sentences.zh: 在城中，執而殺之。

translations.literal: While in the city, he was seized and executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was seized in the city and put to death.

sentences.zh: 阿疏復訴於遼。

translations.literal: Ashu again appealed to the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Ashu again petitioned the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 遼遣奚節度使乙烈來。

translations.literal: The Liao sent the Xi military commissioner Yilie.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao dispatched Yilie, military commissioner of the Xi.

sentences.zh: 穆宗至來流水興和村，見乙烈。

translations.literal: The Mournful Ancestor went to Xinghe Village on the Lailiu River and met Yilie.
translations.idiomatic: The Mournful Ancestor went to Xinghe Village on the Lailiu River to meet Yilie.

sentences.zh: 問阿疏城事，命穆宗曰：「凡攻城所獲，存者復與之，不存者備償。

translations.literal: Inquiring about the matter of Ashu City, he commanded the Mournful Ancestor: “Whatever is taken in storming a city—survivors shall be restored; the dead shall be fully compensated.
translations.idiomatic: Yilie questioned him about Ashu City and commanded: “All who were taken in the siege and still live must be returned; the dead must be paid for in full.

sentences.zh: 」且征馬數百匹。

translations.literal: ” He also demanded several hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: ” He also levied several hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 穆宗與僚佐謀曰：「若償阿疏，則諸部不復可號令任使也。

translations.literal: The Mournful Ancestor consulted his officers, saying: “If we compensate Ashu, the tribes will no longer be subject to our orders and commands.
translations.idiomatic: The Mournful Ancestor consulted his staff: “If we make restitution to Ashu, the tribes will never again heed our authority.

sentences.zh: 」乃令主隈、禿答兩水之民陽爲阻絕鷹路，復使鱉故德部節度使言于遼曰：「欲開鷹路，非生女直節度使不可。

translations.literal: ” He therefore had the peoples of the Zhuwei and Tudai rivers pretend to block the hawk route, and again had the military commissioner of the Biegu’de tribe report to the Liao: “To reopen the hawk route, none but the raw Jurchen military commissioner will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: ” He had the Zhuwei and Tudai river peoples feign obstruction of the hawk route, and sent the Biegu’de military commissioner to tell the Liao: “Only the raw Jurchen military commissioner can reopen the hawk route.

sentences.zh: 」遼不知其爲穆宗謀也，信之，命穆宗討阻絕鷹路者，而阿疏城事遂止。

translations.literal: ” The Liao did not know this was the Mournful Ancestor’s stratagem; they believed it, ordered the Mournful Ancestor to punish those blocking the hawk route, and the matter of Ashu City was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Liao, unaware this was the Mournful Ancestor’s design, believed him, ordered him to suppress the hawk-route obstruction, and the Ashu City affair was shelved.

sentences.zh: 穆宗聲言平鷹路，畋于土溫水而歸。

translations.literal: The Mournful Ancestor announced that he was pacifying the hawk route, hunted on the Tumen River, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Mournful Ancestor proclaimed that he was clearing the hawk route, hunted on the Tumen River, and returned.

sentences.zh: 是歲，留可來降。

translations.literal: That year Liu-ke came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Liu-ke submitted.

sentences.zh: 八年辛巳，遼使使持賜物來賞平鷹路之有功者。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, xinsi, Liao envoys brought gifts to reward those who had meritoriously pacified the hawk route.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1101) Liao envoys arrived with gifts to reward those who had cleared the hawk route.

sentences.zh: 九年壬午，使蒲家奴以遼賜，給主隈、禿答之民，且修鷹路而歸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, renyang, he sent Pujianu to distribute the Liao gifts among the peoples of Zhuwei and Tudai, repair the hawk route, and return.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1102) he sent Pujianu to distribute the Liao largesse among the Zhuwei and Tudai peoples, restore the hawk route, and return.

sentences.zh: 冬，蕭海里叛，入於系案女直阿典部，遣其族人斡達剌來給結和，曰：「願與太師爲友，同往伐遼。

translations.literal: In winter Xiao Haili rebelled and entered the Aidian tribe of the Xi’an Jurchen; he sent his clansman Wodala to propose an alliance, saying: “I wish to be friends with the Grand Master and march together against the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Xiao Haili rebelled and took refuge with the Aidian tribe of the Xi’an Jurchen; he sent his kinsman Wodala to propose an alliance: “Let us be friends, Grand Master, and march together against the Liao.

sentences.zh: 」穆宗執斡達剌。

translations.literal: ” The Mournful Ancestor seized Wodala.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Mournful Ancestor seized Wodala.

sentences.zh: 會遼命穆宗捕討海里，穆宗送斡達剌於遼，募軍得甲千餘。

translations.literal: As it happened the Liao ordered the Mournful Ancestor to capture and punish Haili; the Mournful Ancestor sent Wodala to the Liao and recruited troops, obtaining more than a thousand armored men.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao then ordered the Mournful Ancestor to hunt down Haili; he delivered Wodala to the Liao and mustered troops, raising more than a thousand armored warriors.

sentences.zh: 女直甲兵之數，始見於此，蓋未嘗滿千也。

translations.literal: The number of Jurchen armored troops appears here for the first time—they had never before reached a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first recorded count of Jurchen armored troops—they had never before numbered a thousand.

sentences.zh: 軍次混同水，蕭海里再使人來，復執之。

translations.literal: The army halted at the Huntong River; Xiao Haili again sent envoys, who were again seized.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped on the Huntong River; Xiao Haili sent envoys again, and they too were taken.

sentences.zh: 既而與海里遇。

translations.literal: Before long they encountered Haili.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they met Haili in the field.

sentences.zh: 海里遙問曰：「我使者安在？

translations.literal: Haili called from afar: “Where is my envoy?
translations.idiomatic: Haili shouted from a distance: “Where is my envoy?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「與後人偕來。

translations.literal: ” The reply was: “They came together with those who followed after.
translations.idiomatic: ” The answer came: “They came along with those who followed behind.

sentences.zh: 」海里不信。

translations.literal: ” Haili did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Haili did not believe them.

sentences.zh: 是時，遼追海里兵數千人，攻之不能克。

translations.literal: At this time several thousand Liao troops pursuing Haili attacked but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Liao troops were then pursuing Haili; they attacked but could not break him.

sentences.zh: 穆宗謂遼將曰：「退爾軍，我當獨取海里。

translations.literal: The Mournful Ancestor said to the Liao general: “Withdraw your army; I shall take Haili alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Mournful Ancestor told the Liao commander: “Pull back your men—I will take Haili myself.

sentences.zh: 」遼將許之。

translations.literal: ” The Liao general agreed.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Liao commander consented.

sentences.zh: 太祖策馬突戰，流矢中海里首，海里墮馬下，執而殺之，大破其軍。

translations.literal: Taizu spurred his horse and charged into battle; a flying arrow struck Haili in the head, Haili fell from his horse, was seized and killed, and his army was routed utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu spurred his horse into the melee; a stray arrow struck Haili in the head, he tumbled from the saddle, was seized and killed, and his army was shattered.

sentences.zh: 使阿離合懣獻馘於遼。

translations.literal: He sent Alihemen to present severed heads to the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Alihemen was sent to present the severed heads to the Liao.

sentences.zh: 金人自此知遼兵之易與也。

translations.literal: From this time the Jin people knew how easily the Liao army could be handled.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the Jurchen knew how soft a foe the Liao army could be.

sentences.zh: 是役也，康宗最先登，於是以先登並有功者爲前行，次以諸軍護俘獲歸所部。

translations.literal: In this campaign the Kang Ancestor was first to scale the walls; those who were first over and those who had merit formed the vanguard, and thereafter the various armies escorted captives and booty back to their own tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In that fight the Kang Ancestor was first over the wall; the first climbers and other men of merit formed the vanguard, and the main columns then escorted prisoners and plunder home to their tribes.

sentences.zh: 穆宗朝遼主於漁所，大被嘉賞，授以使相，錫予加等。

translations.literal: The Mournful Ancestor attended upon the Liao sovereign at the fishing grounds, was richly praised, and was invested as envoy-minister, with extraordinary gifts bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The Mournful Ancestor attended the Liao emperor at the fishing grounds, was lavishly praised, invested as commissioner-minister, and showered with exceptional gifts.

sentences.zh: 十年癸未二月，穆宗還。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, guiwei, second month, the Mournful Ancestor returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the tenth year (1103) the Mournful Ancestor returned home.

sentences.zh: 遼使使授從破海里者官賞。

translations.literal: Liao envoys came to grant offices and rewards to those who had joined in defeating Haili.
translations.idiomatic: Liao envoys arrived to confer offices and rewards on those who had helped defeat Haili.

sentences.zh: 高麗始來通好。

translations.literal: Goryeo first sent envoys to establish friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo opened relations for the first time.

sentences.zh: 十月二十九日，穆宗卒，年五十有一。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month the Mournful Ancestor died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month the Mournful Ancestor died, aged fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 初，諸部各有信牌，穆宗用太祖議，擅置牌號者置於法，自是號令乃一，民聽不疑矣。

translations.literal: Earlier the various tribes each had their own tally-tokens; the Mournful Ancestor, following Taizu’s counsel, punished by law anyone who presumptuously issued tally-designations, and from this time commands were unified and the people obeyed without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly each tribe kept its own tally-tokens; acting on Taizu’s advice, the Mournful Ancestor made unauthorized issuance of tokens a capital offense, and from then on orders were one and the people obeyed without question.

sentences.zh: 自景祖以來，兩世四主，志業相因，卒定離析，一切治以本部法令，東南至於乙離骨、曷懶、耶懶、土骨論，東北至於五國、主隈、禿答，金蓋盛於此。

translations.literal: From the Accomplished Ancestor onward, two generations and four rulers, their aims and achievements building on one another, at last consolidated the fragmentation; all was governed by the tribal laws of the home branch—southeast to Yiligu, Helan, Yelan, and Tugulun, northeast to the Five States, Zhuwei, and Tudai—and the Jin reached its height in this age.
translations.idiomatic: From the Accomplished Ancestor through two generations and four lords, purpose piled upon purpose until the scattered tribes were knit into one; all were ruled by the laws of the home branch—from Yiligu, Helan, Yelan, and Tugulun in the southeast to the Five States, Zhuwei, and Tudai in the northeast—and the Jin stood at its zenith.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，追諡孝平皇帝，廟號穆宗。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously titled Emperor Xiaoping, with the temple name Mournful Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he received the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoping, with the temple name Mournful Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏曰獻陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named Xian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong his tomb was designated Xian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡章順孝平皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his posthumous title was augmented to Emperor Zhangshun Xiaoping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was expanded to Emperor Zhangshun Xiaoping.

sentences.zh: 兄子康宗，諱烏雅束，字毛路完，世祖長子也。

translations.literal: His elder brother’s son, the Kang Ancestor, taboo name Wuyashu, courtesy name Maolúwan, was the World Ancestor’s eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew, the Kang Ancestor—whose name was Wuyashu and whose courtesy name was Maolúwan—was the World Ancestor’s eldest son.

sentences.zh: 遼清甯七年辛丑歲生。

translations.literal: Born in the xinchou year, the seventh year of Liao Qingning.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the xinchou year of Liao Qingning’s seventh year (1061).

sentences.zh: 乾統三年癸未，襲節度使，年四十三。

translations.literal: In the third year of Liao Qianyuan, guiwei, he inherited the military commissionership, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Liao Qianyuan (1103) he inherited the military commissionership, aged forty-three.

sentences.zh: 穆宗末年，阿疏使達紀誘扇邊民，曷懶甸人執送之。

translations.literal: In the last years of the Mournful Ancestor, Ashu sent Daji to incite the frontier peoples; the people of Helan district seized and delivered him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Mournful Ancestor’s last years Ashu sent Daji to stir up the border tribes; the people of Helan district seized him and turned him over.

sentences.zh: 穆宗使石適歡撫納曷懶甸，未行，穆宗卒，至是遣焉。

translations.literal: The Mournful Ancestor had Shi Shihuan pacify and receive the Helan district, but before he could depart the Mournful Ancestor died; now he was dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: The Mournful Ancestor had ordered Shi Shihuan to pacify Helan district, but died before he could set out; now the mission was sent.

sentences.zh: 先是，高麗通好，既而頗有隙，高麗使來請議事，使者至高麗，拒而不納。

translations.literal: Earlier friendly relations had been established with Goryeo, but afterward there were considerable frictions; Goryeo sent envoys requesting a conference, but when envoys reached Goryeo they were refused admission.
translations.idiomatic: Relations with Goryeo had begun amicably, but friction soon followed; Goryeo asked for talks, yet when envoys reached Goryeo they were turned away.

sentences.zh: 五水之民附於高麗，執團練使十四人。

translations.literal: The people of the Five Waters sided with Goryeo and seized fourteen regimental trainers.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Waters tribes went over to Goryeo and captured fourteen regimental trainers.

sentences.zh: 語在《高麗傳》中。

translations.literal: The account is in the “Biography of Goryeo.”
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the “Biography of Goryeo.”

sentences.zh: 二年甲申，高麗再來伐，石適歡再破之。

translations.literal: In the second year, jiashen, Goryeo again came to attack, and Shi Shihuan again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1104) Goryeo attacked again, and Shi Shihuan routed them once more.

sentences.zh: 高麗復請和，前所執團練十四人皆遣歸，石適歡撫定邊民而還。

translations.literal: Goryeo again sued for peace; the fourteen regimental trainers previously seized were all sent back, and Shi Shihuan pacified the frontier peoples and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo sued for peace again; all fourteen captured regimental trainers were returned, and Shi Shihuan settled the border peoples and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蘇濱水民不聽命，使斡帶至活羅海川，召諸官僚告諭之。

translations.literal: The Subin River peoples would not obey orders; he sent Wodai to the Huoluo Sea River, summoned the various officials, and admonished them.
translations.idiomatic: The Subin River tribes refused obedience; Wodai was sent to the Huoluo Sea River to summon the local officers and read them the court’s orders.

sentences.zh: 含國部蘇濱水居斡豁勃堇不至。

translations.literal: Wohuo, chief of the Subin River dwellers in the Hanguo tribe, did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Wohuo, chief of the Hanguo Subin River settlement, did not appear.

sentences.zh: 斡准部、職德部既至，復亡去。

translations.literal: The Wozhun and Zhide tribes arrived but then fled again.
translations.idiomatic: The Wozhun and Zhide tribes came, then bolted again.

sentences.zh: 塢塔遇二部于馬紀嶺，執之而來，遂伐斡豁，克之。

translations.literal: Wuta encountered the two tribes at Maji Ridge, seized them and brought them in, then campaigned against Wohuo and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuta intercepted the two tribes at Maji Ridge, took them captive, then marched against Wohuo and overran him.

sentences.zh: 斡帶進至北琴海，攻拔泓忒城，乃還。

translations.literal: Wodai advanced to the North Qin Sea, stormed and took Hongte City, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wodai pushed on to the North Qin Sea, stormed Hongte City, and returned.

sentences.zh: 四年丙戌，高麗遣黑歡方石來賀襲位，遣杯魯報之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, bingxu, Goryeo sent Heihuan Fangshi to congratulate him on his succession to office; he dispatched Beilu in return.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1106) Goryeo sent Heihuan Fangshi to congratulate him on assuming the commissionership; Beilu was sent in reply.

sentences.zh: 高麗約還諸亡在彼者，乃使阿聒、勝昆往受之。

translations.literal: Goryeo had promised to return all fugitives on its side; he then sent Asui and Shengkun to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo had pledged to return those who had fled to its territory; he dispatched Asui and Shengkun to take charge of them.

sentences.zh: 高麗背約，殺二使，築九城於曷懶甸，以兵數萬來攻。

translations.literal: Goryeo broke the agreement, killed the two envoys, built nine fortresses in the Halian district, and came to attack with tens of thousands of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo violated the pact, executed both envoys, erected nine fortresses in the Halian region, and marched against the Jurchen with an army of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 斡賽敗之。

translations.literal: Wosai defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wosai routed their forces.

sentences.zh: 斡魯亦築九城，與高麗九城相對。

translations.literal: Wolu likewise built nine fortresses, facing Goryeo’s nine fortresses across from them.
translations.idiomatic: Wolu built nine counter-fortresses to stand opposite Goryeo’s nine.

sentences.zh: 高麗復來攻，斡賽復敗之。

translations.literal: Goryeo attacked again, and Wosai again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Goryeo attacked once more, Wosai defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 高麗約以還逋逃之人，退九城之軍。

translations.literal: Goryeo agreed to return the fugitives and withdrew the army from the nine fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo agreed to surrender the fugitives and pull back the garrisons from the nine fortresses.

sentences.zh: 復所侵故地。

translations.literal: They also restored the territory that had been seized.
translations.idiomatic: The lands that had been seized were restored as well.

sentences.zh: 九月，乃罷兵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month they finally ceased hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: Hostilities ceased in the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 七年己丑，歲不登，減盜賊征償，振貧乏者。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, jichou, the harvest failed; blood-price levies for theft were reduced and the poor were relieved.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, jichou, when crops failed, blood-price payments for theft were lowered and the destitute were aided.

sentences.zh: 十一年癸巳，康宗卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, guisi, the Kang Ancestor died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, guisi, the Kang Ancestor died at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，追諡恭簡皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he was posthumously titled Emperor Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he received the posthumous title Emperor Gongjian.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，號其藏曰喬陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong his burial mound was named Qiao Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong his tomb was designated Qiao Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 五年，增諡康宗獻敏恭簡皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his posthumous title was augmented to Kang Ancestor Emperor Xianmin Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his posthumous title was expanded to Kang Ancestor Emperor Xianmin Gongjian.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金之厥初，兄弟三人，亦微矣。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: At the very beginning of the Jin, the three brothers were likewise insignificant.
translations.idiomatic: The chronicler remarks: In the Jin’s earliest days, three brothers alone were its whole beginning—and that beginning was humble indeed.

sentences.zh: 熙宗追帝祖宗，定著始祖、景祖、世祖廟，世世不祧。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong traced the imperial ancestors and fixed the temples of the Founding Ancestor, Accomplished Ancestor, and World Ancestor, never to be displaced in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong established the ancestral temples of the Founding Ancestor, Accomplished Ancestor, and World Ancestor, which were never to be removed from the sacrificial order.

sentences.zh: 始祖娶六十之婦而生二男一女，豈非天耶？

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor married a woman of sixty and begot two sons and one daughter—was this not Heaven’s doing?
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor wed a woman of sixty and fathered two sons and a daughter—could this have been anything but Heaven’s design?

sentences.zh: 景祖不受遼籍遼印，取雅達國相以與其子。

translations.literal: The Accomplished Ancestor would not enter Liao registers or accept a Liao seal, and took the office of state minister from Yada to give to his son.
translations.idiomatic: The Accomplished Ancestor refused Liao enrollment and the Liao seal, yet secured the state-ministership from Yada for his son.

sentences.zh: 世祖既破桓赧、散達，遼政日衰，而以太祖屬之穆宗，其思慮豈不深遠矣夫！

translations.literal: After the World Ancestor had broken Huanran and Sandá, Liao governance daily declined; that he entrusted Taizu to the Mournful Ancestor—how far-reaching was that design!
translations.idiomatic: Once the World Ancestor had shattered Huanran and Sandá, Liao power waned day by day; to place Taizu in the Mournful Ancestor’s keeping was foresight of rare depth indeed.
